title: What Happens When a Member Accepts or Purchases a Lead?
content: What Happens When a Member Accepts or Purchases a Lead? Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007988 When a lead is submitted through the website, members receive a lead notification email containing a preview of the inquiry. The lead's contact information is hidden until the member accepts or purchases the lead, depending on the website's lead settings. The notification email includes an " Accept Lead " link that automatically logs the member into their account and directs them to the lead details page. For free leads, members can click the Accept button to instantly reveal the lead's contact information, including the email address and phone number. When a member accepts a lead, the site administrator receives a notification. This provides an opportunity to follow up with the member, confirm they were able to access the lead successfully, and discuss any available membership upgrades or premium features. For paid leads, members are prompted to purchase the lead from their Member Dashboard before accessing the contact information. Once payment is completed successfully, the lead's email address and phone number become immediately available, allowing the member to contact the lead directly. The site administrator is also notified when a lead purchase is completed. Related Articles: >> Purchasing Leads

title: What Happens If A Lead Is Not Accepted?
content: What Happens If A Lead Is Not Accepted? Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007989 Brilliant Directories provides tools to help directory owners track leads that have not been accepted by members. Monitoring unaccepted leads helps ensure that website visitors receive responses to their inquiries and allows administrators to take appropriate follow-up actions when needed. When a lead is not accepted by a member, consider following up with the website visitor to ensure their inquiry is addressed. Possible next steps include: • Offering to match the visitor with other qualified businesses or professionals. • Reviewing whether additional members should receive the lead. • Ensuring the visitor has alternative options available through the directory. Following up with the member who declined the lead can provide valuable insight into why the lead was not accepted. Common reasons may include: • The member is not accepting new clients. • The lead falls outside the member's service area. • The lead does not match the member's services. • The member is temporarily unavailable. Understanding these reasons can help improve future lead distribution and member engagement. To receive notifications when a member declines a lead, enable the Lead Declined Notification setting. Navigation: Leads » Lead Settings » Auto-Match Workflows » Additional Notifications Settings

title: How Should I Follow Up With A Lead?
content: How Should I Follow Up With A Lead? Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007990 A lead is generated when a visitor contacts a business or professional through the directory website. Leads provide members with opportunities to connect with potential customers and generate new business. For directory owners, each lead also creates an opportunity to engage with members, demonstrate the value of the website, and strengthen long-term member relationships. For newer directory websites, it is recommended to personally follow up with members who receive leads. A quick phone call or email can help ensure that the member successfully received the lead and understands how to access their account and lead information. Direct communication with members can help build trust and improve member retention. During the conversation, consider: • Confirming that the lead was received successfully. • Answering any questions about the platform. • Explaining available features and benefits. • Gathering feedback about the member's experience. Follow-up conversations can also provide an opportunity to introduce premium membership benefits when appropriate. Rather than focusing on a sales pitch, concentrate on understanding the member's needs and explaining how additional features may help them generate more value from the directory. After a member accepts or purchases a lead, consider following up within the next 24 to 48 hours. This follow-up can help: • Confirm that the member successfully contacted the lead. • Identify any questions or issues. • Gather feedback about the lead quality. • Strengthen the relationship between the member and the directory.

title: How To Manage Leads Sent To Claim Listings
content: How To Manage Leads Sent To Claim Listings Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007991 Imported Claim Listings often contain outdated or missing contact information. While Claim Listings help populate a directory and improve credibility, they may still receive inquiries and leads from visitors. When a lead is submitted to a Claim Listing, the listing owner may never receive the notification if the email address on file is incorrect. This article explains the recommended process for managing leads sent to Claim Listings and converting those listings into active members. In our Ultimate Guide On Claim Listings we explain that Claim Listings should be used primarily to give the website credibility and provide search results for the visitors. Claim Listings can receive leads even if they have not been claimed by the business owner. In many cases, visitors discover these listings through search engines and submit inquiries directly through the directory website. When this happens, it creates an opportunity to engage the business owner and encourage them to claim or activate their listing. When a Claim Listing receives a lead the recommendation is to: 1. Search online for the business's current email address and phone number. 2. Update the listing with the correct contact information. 3. Move the listing to a separate membership level dedicated to Claim Listings that have received leads. This makes it easier to identify and follow up with businesses that have already demonstrated interest from directory visitors. After updating the listing's contact information, resend the lead notification from the Admin Dashboard. This step is important because the original notification may have been sent to an outdated or invalid email address. After resending the lead notification, contact the business owner directly. The objectives of the call are: • Confirm that the business owner received the lead notification email. • Help them access their account. • Encourage them to claim and manage their listing. Since the lead notification email contains access to the member account, the business owner should immediately secure the account by updating the password. During the call: 1. Ask the business owner to open the lead notification email. 2. Have them click the link included in the email. 3. Navigate to Account >> Change Password. 4. Assist them in creating a new password. For detailed instructions, refer to: Changing a Members Password After the business owner has successfully accessed the account, manually move the member from the Claim Listing membership level to the appropriate active membership level. This ensures the listing is no longer treated as an unclaimed profile. If the business owner is not interested in managing the listing: • Remove the listing from the directory. • Follow up with the lead submitter. • Offer to connect them with alternative businesses listed on the website. Important Note : Claim listing emails with that contain only numbers @ the Email Domain of the site will not be  automatically matched to lead emails. (E.g: 1234@yoursite.com ) To resend a lead access Interactions >> Member Leads >> Find the lead, click on Actions >> Match Lead Scroll down and look for Matched Members , hover the mouse on top of the Name of the member and click on Send Lead Preview Email.

title: What Is Additional Matching?
content: What Is Additional Matching? Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007993 Additional Matching allows directory owners to manually send a lead to additional members after the lead has been submitted. This feature can be used with leads generated from both Member Contact Forms and Get Matched Forms, providing greater flexibility when connecting visitors with relevant businesses or professionals. With the Basic Lead package included in every Brilliant Directories license, administrators can manually match leads to additional members within the directory. Manual matching provides complete control over which members receive a lead, making it a reliable option for directories that require accuracy and oversight when distributing inquiries. Related Articles: » How to Match a Lead » The Member Contact Form » How to Match Leads To Members » The Get Matched Form

title: What Is The Automatic Lead Matching Add-On?
content: What Is The Automatic Lead Matching Add-On? Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007994 Overview All directory websites generate leads from visitors who contact professional members. This add-on allows the site to instantly send leads to members without manually matching them. This means members will automatically be connected with leads and have the ability to purchase them in real-time. The website will generate more revenue from leads than ever before! How To Get This Add-On Websites with the VIP Add-Ons Club automatically have this add-on available: Join The VIP Add-Ons Club Purchase Individually: Automatic Lead Matching Add-On How It Works This add-on enhances the default Leads system included with all sites by introducing advanced settings and automated matching tools that help speed up lead processing. By default, leads submitted through the "Get Matched" form are marked as Pending and require manual review by an admin—a task that can become overwhelming when submissions start piling up. How to Match a Lead » Get Matched Form With the auto-matching feature enabled, the system can automatically match leads based on the request details, saving time and reducing the need for hands-on management. It’s important to note that auto-matching only applies to leads submitted through the "Get Matched" form—typically found at /getmatched—and only if the visitor requests replies from multiple members. Leads sent directly to a specific member are not auto-matched, though they can still be auto-delivered using a separate setting. Enable "Get Replies from more members?" Option This feature is ideal for websites receiving a high volume of leads and looking to reduce manual work. For new or low-volume sites, we generally recommend sticking with the default leads system until there's a need for more automation. Review the entire documentation folder for more information: >> Automatic Lead Matching Add-On Folder Additional Settings This add-on introduces three additional options to the Leads Settings dropdown, giving more control over how leads are handled. General Settings Each additional option is explained in the following section: Lead Settings » General Settings Auto-Match & Create New Workflow Each setting is explained in the following section: Default Lead Action & Creating New Lead Actions

title: Benefits & Limitations Of The Automatic Lead Matching Add-On
content: Benefits & Limitations Of The Automatic Lead Matching Add-On Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000007995 The following documentation is exclusively for the "Auto-Matching or Advanced Leads Package". To purchase the "Auto-Matching or Advanced Leads Package". >> Automatic Lead Matching Benefits Of Auto-Matching More time Eliminate the need to manually match leads to additional members. Set the maximum number of leads that can be sent for every lead entry For example, set it so that up to 10 members can be sent an email notifying them of a new lead. Set the maximum number of lead acceptance This ensures that the website visitors do not get contacted by dozens of members. Such an experience would be considered as “spam” by most. By setting the limit to “3” for example, the site could technically send out the lead to 50 members but only have a maximum of 3 that can contact the website visitor. More time to focus on marketing The less manual tasks that the team need to complete, the more focus can be used on marketing and sales. Limitations Of Auto-Matching Lower Quality Of Leads There is no way to prevent a solicitation or poor lead from being sent to the members with the auto-matching turned on. Expert Tip Never charge for leads if the auto-matching turned on. Paying for a poor lead is the fastest way to lose members.

title: Member Leads » Lead Settings » Receiving Direct Leads Settings
content: Member Leads » Lead Settings » Receiving Direct Leads Settings Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008054 To edit the general settings for " Receiving Direct Leads " when using the Basic Leads package go to: Interactions » Member Leads » Lead Settings and click on " Receiving Direct Leads ": Available Settings In The Basic Leads Module: Members Receive Direct Leads Immediately: When enabled, leads submitted through a member’s profile page are delivered to the member immediately. When disabled, an administrator must review the lead and manually assign it to the member. Member Notification Type: Select " Preview " to send the member who received the lead a portion (preview) of the information submitted in the lead, rather than all of the information submitted in the lead. This preview will typically contain the content of the lead, but will not contain the contact information (phone and email) of the person who submitted the lead. Members will have to accept or purchase the lead in order to see the complete information of the lead. Select " Complete " to send all of the information submitted in the lead immediately without the need to accept or purchase the lead. Recommended: Use Preview to follow lead management best practices. Label Direct Lead As: Select " Accepted " for this match to count against the "Maximum Acceptances" total set in the General Lead Settings tab. Select " Pending " for this match to not count against the "Maximum Acceptances" total set in the General Lead Settings tab. Preview Email Template: Sends the member a limited preview of the lead details, typically excluding contact information such as email and phone number. Members must accept or purchase the lead to view the full submission. Complete Email Template: Select the email template to send to the member if "Complete" is selected above. Copy Admin On This Email: Send a copy of the "Preview Email Template" or "Complete Email Template" to the Admin email address(es) when it is sent to a member. Where can members view their leads: Once a member logs into their account, on the dashboard, they will be able to see the new leads on the " M anage Leads " option: Additional Information: » Leads » Lead Emails » Purchasing Leads

title: Member Leads » Lead Settings » Additional Notifications Settings
content: Member Leads » Lead Settings » Additional Notifications Settings Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008056 To configure the general Additional Notifications settings when using the default lead system (without the Auto Match Leads add-on enabled), navigate to: Interactions » Member Leads » Lead Settings and click on " Additional Notifications ": The Additional Notifications settings include two tabs: Admin – Controls notifications sent to website administrators. Visitor – Controls notifications sent to the user who submits the lead form. The Visitor refers to the website user who submits a lead form. Available Settings In Additional Notifications Admin: Email Admin When Lead Submitted: Enable this setting to send an email notification to the configured admin email address whenever a lead is submitted on the website. Admin Lead Submitted Template: Choose the email template that will be sent to administrators when Email Admin When Lead Submitted is enabled. Visitor: Email Visitor After Lead Submission: Enable this setting to automatically send an email to the visitor after they submit a lead. Visitor Email Template: Choose the email template sent to visitors when Email Visitor After Lead Submission is enabled. Copy Admin On This Email?: Enable this option to send administrators a copy of the visitor notification email when Email Visitor After Lead Submission is enabled. Visitor Email Variable: This setting specifies the form field variable that stores the visitor’s email address.When Email Visitor After Lead Submission is enabled, the selected visitor email template will be sent to the email address submitted in this field. The default value is lead_email , and it is recommended to leave this setting unchanged for most websites. Settings In Additional Notifications for Custom Actions If the Automatic Lead Matching Add-On is active on the site the admin will be able to create custom lead actions . When a lead is submitted through a form that is not associated with a specific member (for example, the /getmatched page), all Lead Submitted notifications will be controlled by the Main Action . If additional custom actions are configured, their Lead Submitted notification settings will only apply to direct leads submitted to members assigned to the membership plans selected for that action. The affected membership plans can be configured in the General Settings tab of the custom action.

title: The Email Variables Used with the  Leads Module
content: The Email Variables Used with the Leads Module Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008058 The Leads Module includes several variables that can be used when creating or customizing lead-related email templates. These variables allow you to automatically insert lead information, member details, login links, and other dynamic content into your emails. The following variables power the Basic Lead Module, and can be used when creating custom lead emails. Important note: When using lead variables, make sure to enter them exactly as shown below. Some variables require a single percentage sign (%variable%), while others require three percentage signs (%%%variable%%%). Using the wrong format may prevent the variable from displaying correctly in the email. For more information about variables, please see: » Understanding Variables Variables Member Access Variables These variables help members quickly access their account or view a lead. %member_login_link% Automatically logs the member into their dashboard without requiring them to enter their username or password. %member_lead_match_link% Takes the member directly to the specific lead associated with the email without requiring them to log in manually. This is the recommended variable for lead notification emails because it provides the fastest way for members to review, accept, or purchase leads. Lead Information Variables These variables display information submitted by the website visitor when creating the lead. %%%details%%% Displays the lead information fields configured in the Get Matched form. The information displayed by this variable can be customized by editing the fields included in the Get Matched form. %%%lead_id%%% Displays the Lead ID number. This is commonly used in administrative notifications to make it easier to locate a specific lead within the admin area. %%%lead_name%%% Displays the name of the website visitor who submitted the lead. %%%lead_email%%% Displays the email address entered by the website visitor. Important: This variable will display the visitor's email address even if the lead is configured as a Preview Lead. For this reason, it is typically only used in emails sent to the website visitor and is not included in member lead notification emails by default. %%%lead_phone%%% Displays the phone number entered by the website visitor. Like the lead email variable, this will display the phone number regardless of whether the lead is set to Preview or Complete. %%%lead_location%%% Displays the location entered by the website visitor when submitting the lead. Member Information Variables These variables display information about the member who was matched with the lead. %%%full_name%%% Displays the member's name. For Individual Accounts, the member's first and last name will be displayed. For Company Accounts, the company name will be displayed. %%%user_id%%% Displays the member's User ID number. %%%location%%% Displays the location of the matched member. Website Variables %%%website_name%%% Displays the website name. This variable is commonly used in email subject lines and email signatures to reinforce branding and recognition. Security Token Variables These variables return secure system tokens that can be used when creating custom links or integrations. %token% Displays the secure token associated with the lead. %user_token% Displays the secure token associated with the matched member. Custom Login Link Example The following link automatically logs the member into their account and takes them directly to the lead details page: Login to your account to view this lead Additional Information: » How to Edit Email Templates » Emails » Email Templates » New Email Template

title: How to Turn The Brilliant Directories Directory Website into a Mobile Application for Apple & Android
content: How to Turn The Brilliant Directories Directory Website into a Mobile Application for Apple & Android Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008202 The video below shows how to convert a Brilliant Directories website into a mobile app in less than 5 minutes using third-party, no-code app building platforms. The website users will have the same familiar experience on the mobile app as they do on the main Brilliant Directories website. This approach displays your live website inside an app using WebView technology. Starting with a mobile-friendly website saves time and makes the entire app-building process easier. Video Note The app builder shown in the video (Como) was acquired and later shut down. The same WebView-based approach shown in the video still applies to modern no-code app builders. No-Code Method The easiest way to turn a Brilliant Directories website into a mobile app is by using a no-code app builder that supports loading your website inside the app using a WebView. No-code app builders are third-party services and operate independently from Brilliant Directories. They have their own plans, pricing, and publishing requirements. How It Works Your live Brilliant Directories site is displayed inside a mobile app shell. Your homepage loads first, and all navigation, logins, forms, listings, and features work exactly as they do on your website. No content needs to be rebuilt and no code is required. Set your website URL as the app’s homepage, or Add your website as a navigation item within the app Some app builders may show optional menus, screens, or layout tools in their interface. These are not required when using your website as the primary WebView. Limitations This method creates a WebView-based app (a website inside an app). It does not generate a fully custom native mobile app interface. Popular No-Code App Builders Appy Pie Convert your website into Android and iOS apps by entering your site URL. https://www.appypie.com/convert-website-to-mobile-apps BuildFire Embed your website inside the app using the WebView plugin. https://buildfire.com/plugin/webview-2/ GoodBarber Display your website in the app using a URL-based WebView section. https://www.goodbarber.com/help/web-view-sections-r33/url-section-web-view-a27/ NOTE: Any no-code app builder that supports loading a website URL as the app homepage or as a navigation item follows this same general methodology. Advanced Option A fully native mobile app can be built using custom development and the Brilliant Directories API. This approach requires development resources and is outside the scope of no-code app builders. Developer Accounts Publishing a mobile app requires developer accounts with the app stores. These accounts, review processes, and any associated fees are managed directly between you and the app store provider. Apple An Apple Developer account is required to publish apps to the App Store. https://developer.apple.com/support/compare-memberships Google A Google Developer account is required to publish apps to Google Play. http://developer.android.com/distribute/googleplay/start.html

title: How To Manually Bill A Member / Create A Subscription For A Member
content: How To Manually Bill A Member / Create A Subscription For A Member Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008873 At any moment, the site can create a subscription (recurring or one-time payment) for a member of the directory. Keep in mind that when someone signs up from the /join page, the system will create the subscription automatically. However, sometimes the owner wants to change the subscription's amount or create a new subscription. This is also very beneficial if the site is taking external payments (bank transfers, checks, etc.,) instead of accepting direct payments on the site. Create a "New Order" Log in to the admin area and navigate to Members » Search Members. Locate the member and click on Actions » Payment History: At the top right, click on the "New Order" button: Fill out the new order form with the subscription details: Membership Plan: Select the membership plan of this specific order. Billing Cycle: Monthly, Quarterly, Semi-Yearly, and Yearly. (this will depend on the configuration set up in the membership plan) Price Override: Type the new amount for this specific order. Leave this option blank if the membership plan doesn't need to be overridden. Enter a price greater than 0. Start Billing On: By default, the system will show today's date. However, it can be modified to any date in the future. Admin Notes : Add notes for the internal team (See example below). Create Order : The system will save and create the order. Confirm the order by clicking on the "Submit Order" button: The page should load automatically and the message "New Order Created" will appear with an order summary: Card on File If the member had a credit card on file and the date selected was today, then the system should collect the payment. To verify if the money was taken successfully, click on the "Transactions" tab and make sure the status of the order says "Paid". This payment can also be verified under Finance » Transaction History: If the charge couldn't be attempted or there was no card registered to begin with, this means that the credit on file needs to be updated. title: How to Setup Upgrade/Downgrade Options for Membership Plans
content: How to Setup Upgrade/Downgrade Options for Membership Plans Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000008978 The Available Upgrade Options settings control which membership plans appear on the Upgrade/Downgrade page for each member. This guide outlines the steps to enable and configure these settings within a Brilliant Directories website. How to Activate the "Available Upgrade Options" Settings Follow these steps: 1. Go to the Membership Plans Section Navigate to Finance » Membership Plans . Click Edit on the membership plan that requires configuration. 2. Open the Sign Ups & Upgrades Tab Click Sign Ups & Upgrades tab. Scroll down to find the section titled Change Plan – Upgrade/Downgrade Settings . Configuration Options Scroll down in the settings area to find the following options: 1. Upgrade Email Sent Choose an email template to send to members after they upgrade to this membership plan. Additional Option Send Copy of Email to Default Website Email Address If checked (default), the system sends a copy of the upgrade email to the site admin. Email Template Recommendations Upgrade Email (Template: upgrade-response ) Use when upgrading from a lower-tier plan. Downgrade Email (Template: downgrade-response ) Use when moving to a lower-tier plan, especially from the highest-tier plan. Generic Template Create a neutral template if this plan is both an upgrade and downgrade option. This keeps the message relevant regardless of direction. 2. After Upgrading to This Plan, Set Account Status As Choose the member's account status after the upgrade Active Account Member becomes active and visible on the site. Inactive Account Member remains inactive and hidden from the site. Same Status Before Upgrading Member retains the status they had before the upgrade. On Hold, Requires Admin Approval Member is on hold until manually approved by the admin. 3. Available Upgrade Options This is the key setting to control which plans members can upgrade or downgrade to. Available Plans Select the membership plans that should appear as upgrade/downgrade options. Pre-Selected Plan Choose the default selected upgrade option. Display Order Choose the order in which plans appear on the upgrade page. 4. Upgrade Page Header Content Enter a custom message or instruction that will appear above the upgrade options on the member’s Upgrade page. 5. Description Why Members Should Upgrade to This Level Add a description that explains the benefits of upgrading to this plan. This description will only be visible to members who are eligible to upgrade to this plan — not to those who are already on it. Note : This message will not display for members already in the plan. This description will not display for members already enrolled in Plan 1. 6. Free Trial when upgrading If the membership plan a member upgrades to includes a Free Trial, the free trial will also be applied during the upgrade process. This means members upgrading to that plan will receive the same trial period as they would during a new sign-up, according to the membership plan's Free Trial settings and this will show in the member dashboard when upgrading: 7. Card-Based Layout on Member Upgrade Page A new Advanced Setting is available to display the available membership plans in a card view instead of the standard list layout. When enabled, members will see the membership plan options presented as individual cards during the sign-up, upgrade, or downgrade process: Additional Notes Membership plans with the Account Type: "Claim" do not allow plan changes until the listing is claimed by a member. For more information about the member upgrade experience, see: Member Upgrades From Members’ Perception

title: Embed Conversion Tracking and Affiliate Tracking Codes On Sign Up Pages
content: Embed Conversion Tracking and Affiliate Tracking Codes On Sign Up Pages Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000009295 There are many 3rd party tools that require placing a tracking code on "success pages" in order to track sales, sign-ups, conversions, and more. With Brilliant Directories, it is possible to place tracking code widget for the "success pages" into each membership plan or in a specific widget that will apply to all membership plans. Membership Plans Method There is a setting on each membership plan where the widget with the code can be placed. It can be found under Finance >> Membership Plans >> find the membership where the code needs to be added and click on Edit . Navigate to the " Sign-Ups & Upgrades " tab and scroll down to " Sign Ups / Upgrade Conversion Tracking Code " and select the preferred widget: *This allows the activation of an additional Tracking Code Widget that will work alongside the default Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes , which will always remain active. Conversion Tracking Codes Widget and Available Variables to Utilize Navigate Toolbox >> Widget Manager >> Bootstrap Theme - Conversion Tracking Codes An example conversion tracking to add could look like the following: fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "AUD", value: <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>}); This code should be added below the following comment within this widget: When adding this code, please make sure to wrap it around the <script> tag, as shown below: <script type="text/javascript">fbq('track', 'Purchase', {currency: "AUD", value: <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?>});</script> The end result would look like the following: Some common variables that affiliates and other trackers want to be included in the pixel tracking code are the order amount and order or member ID, etc. These are the variables available with Brilliant Directories: COMMON VARIABLES AFFILIATE TRACKERS USE: FIRST PAYMENT AMOUNT = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['amount']; ?> RECURRING PAYMENT AMOUNT = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['recurring_amount']; ?> ORDER ID / MEMBER ID = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['user_id']; ?> COUPON CODE = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['coupon_code']; ?> PRODUCT NAME = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['product_name']; ?> PRODUCT TYPE = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['product_type']; ?> FREE TRIAL = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['free_trial']; ?> FREE TRIAL DAYS = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['free_trial_period']; ?> FIRST BILL DATE = <?php echo $conversion_tracking['first_bill_date']; ?> ADVANCED VARIABLES AFFILIATE TRACKERS USE: $conversion_tracking['invoice']['variable'];    (Invoice Variables from the tblinvoices table) $conversion_tracking['product']['variable'];   (Member Subscription Variables from the tblhosting table) IMPORTANT NOTE: This widget is where the tracking code for affiliate programs, analytics, and more can be placed. This widget only loads on pages after a member sign-ups or upgrades, to track successful sign-ups. Alternative Method: Adding Conversion Tracking to Pop-Up Success Messages If the conversion action does not load a separate success page (e.g., a pop-up message confirms success on the same page), the conversion tracking code can also be placed in the text label that appears after a successful action. This can be done by navigating the Text Label for the post-success message and embedding the tracking code there. For this example, let's add a Google Ads conversion tracking setup for a newsletter subscriber pop-up. To accomplish this, first, navigate Toolbox >> Widget Manager and create a new widget: Name the widget, add the tracking code in the HTML tab, and save the changes: Then copy the PHP shortcode of the widget: Next, place the copied shortcode of the widget to the text label: Alternatively, the code can be inserted directly within the text label. However, we recommend using the widget method for more reliable performance and smoother processing. The tracking code will now trigger each time a user subscribes to the newsletter. This option is especially useful for scenarios where confirmation appears as inline text or a pop-up, rather than a new page. Be sure to use this method as an alternative in any scenario where a separate success page is not available. NOTE : This method may not be optimal and might not work reliably if the script requires a specific loading sequence or is complex. However, it can be effective in many cases. Be sure to thoroughly test before finalizing any updates.

title: How Does Auto-Matching Work? (Lead Settings » General Settings)
content: How Does Auto-Matching Work? (Lead Settings » General Settings) Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000009581 The following documentation is exclusively for the "Auto-Matching or Advanced Leads Package". Auto-matching relies on the auto-matching settings and the search inputs submitted by the users of the website. Here are some of the core concepts of how auto-matching works: The engine will only match members that match the criteria. If the member is allowed to select a location, say San Francisco, and only 2 members are located in San Francisco, only those two candidates will be matched (assuming they match the additional criteria set by the user such as categories). Membership Level Sort Order is taken into consideration. This means if there are three premium members in San Francisco, these three premium members will always be auto-matched ahead of the free members that are also located in San Francisco. For accurate auto-matching, allowing for category inputs and location inputs is key. Not requiring a location or specialty to be entered limits the engine. Essentially the auto-matching functionality is the same as the member search functionality on the website. The system runs a search just like the users would, and starts to auto-match leads always going from top to bottom. Auto-Matching Lead Settings Edit the auto-matching lead settings by going to Leads » Manage Lead » General Settings : Or within the " Auto-Match Workflows " screen: Data Flows Settings There are 5 additional settings for the automatic matching functionality. Search Radius : Members within this radius are eligible to be automatically matched to leads. Maximum Matches: This setting controls how many members can be matched to a single lead. Set this to "3", and a maximum of 3 members will be matched. If no one meets the search criteria, no one will be matched and the lead will be flagged as "Pending". Maximum Acceptances: This controls how many members can accept a lead. This is particularly helpful if the maximum matches is set to 5+ members, but don't want the website users to be bombarded with emails from the visitors. Once the maximum lead acceptance is reached, the lead status will change to "Sold Out". Notify Admin If Member Email Invalid: Select "Yes" if you would like to send an email notification to the Admin when a lead has been matched to a member that does not have a valid email address. Admin Notification Email Template: Select the email template to send to the Admin if a lead is matched to a member that does not have a valid email address.

title: Understanding Actions / Data Flows
content: Understanding Actions / Data Flows Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000009585 This documentation covers features specific to the Automatic Lead Matching add-on. Automatic Lead Matching Add-On What Is It? The Automatic Lead Matching add-on upgrades the default Leads system by introducing customizable Lead Actions—rules that control how leads are handled for different membership levels. The standard Basic Leads Package includes: Instant delivery for direct lead requests Limit on how many members can accept a lead Admin email alerts when new leads come in With this add-on, custom Lead Actions can be created and assigned to individual membership levels, giving full control over how leads are distributed and managed. Key Features: Auto-Match Control: Decide which members can receive leads automatically. Custom Email Templates per Membership Level : Send different email content to free vs. paid members—thank paying members and encourage free users to upgrade. Member Lead Acceptance Alerts : Get notified when a member accepts a lead—ideal timing to follow up or promote upgrades. Automate a thank-you or upsell email. Sold-Out Lead Notifications: Get alerted when a member tries to claim a lead that’s already been sold. Trigger an automatic email explaining what happened and how to avoid it. These features are exclusive to the Automatic Lead Matching add-on and designed to help automate lead distribution while maximizing upsell opportunities and overall lead management efficiency. title: Manually Approve New Member Signups
content: Manually Approve New Member Signups Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000010781 This article explains the step-by-step process for manually approving new members. The platform allows configuring member approval settings for each membership plan. To enable this functionality for each membership plan, follow the instructions below: 1. Go to Finance » Membership Plans. 2. Find the membership plan and click "Edit" Manually approving 'General User' or 'Free' membership plans is highly recommended. Click Actions » Quick Edit. 4. Change the "Account Status" to "Active Account", and save the changes. When the status is 'On Hold' and it is changed to 'Active', the system prompts the administrator to send an email notification. NOTE: The email template sent above is called: user-approved-by-admin . It can be found under Emails » Email Templates. The member's status will now be 'Active. As soon as the status changes, the member will be visible on the front end of the website.

title: Managing Member Credit Cards
content: Managing Member Credit Cards Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000011521 This article covers how to do the following from the Admin area of the site: How to check if a member currently has a credit card on file. How to add a credit card for a member. How to update the credit card on file for a member. How to delete a credit card on file for a member. To do any of the above actions, follow these steps: Click My Members » Search Members Search for the member and click Actions » Payment History: Click the "CC Info" button: Checking if a Member Has a Credit Card on File If the member has a credit card on file, a snippet of the credit card information will display here: Adding a Credit Card for a Member Click the "Add Credit Card" button: Enter the credit card information of the member: Click the "Save credit card & continue" button. If the complete credit card information is entered with no errors, a success message like this will appear: Click the "Close Window" button. The member's credit card information on file will be displayed here: Understanding Card Type Information (Stripe Only) When an admin views a member’s saved payment information in the member’s Account Details , the dashboard will also display the type of card stored for that account. This information is only available when when Stripe is used as the payment gateway. Other gateways do not display these details. The card type label helps clarify how the card is stored in Stripe and whether it supports recurring subscription payments. Below are the possible types and their meanings: Legacy A non-3D Secure card saved as a legacy “card” object in Stripe. Recurring subscription payments will process normally. If there are any issues collecting payments on this type of card, the member may need to log in to the Member Dashboard and save their credit card information once again so it is saved as a modern "Payment Method" object in Stripe. Legacy (3DS) A 3D Secure card saved as a legacy “card” object in Stripe . If there are any issues collecting payments on this type of card, the member may need to log in to the Member Dashboard and save their credit card information once again so it is saved as a modern "Payment Method" object in Stripe. Payment Method A non-3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe. This is Stripe's preferred, most up-to-date format. Recurring subscription payments will process normally. Payment Method (3DS Recurring) A 3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe that supports recurring subscription payments. Recurring subscription payments will process normally. Payment Method (3DS Manual) A 3D Secure card saved as a modern “payment method” object in Stripe that requires manual authentication for each transaction. The member must log in to their Member Dashboard and manually authenticate every payment. The member may contact the bank to remove this requirement or use a different card. Updating a Member’s Credit Card on File To update the credit card on file for a member, click the "Update" button: NOTE: This button will only appear if the member already has a credit card on file. The current credit card on file will appear at the top of the modal. The fields for entering the updated information will also appear there: Click the "Save credit card & continue" button. If the complete credit card information is entered with no errors , a success message like this will display: Click the "Close Window" button.  The updated credit card information will be reflected on the following page: Updating a Member’s Credit Card on File Click the "Clear" button: Confirm removal of the credit card on file by clicking the "Yes, clear credit card" button: Once successfully deleted, a success message will appear, click the "Close Window" button: Customizing Member Credit Card Form Text Labels The text labels displayed in the pop-up for adding or updating a member’s credit card can be modified in the Admin area. This is useful for aligning terminology with business requirements or providing clearer instructions to members. To update these labels: Navigate to Settings >> Text Labels in the Admin menu. Search for terms related to the credit card form, such as: 1. add_credit_card_popup_title 2. add_credit_card_popup_subtitle (hidden) 3. cc_card_name 4. cc_card_number 5. cc_expiration_date 6. cc_security_code Edit the desired text labels and save the changes. Once updated, the new labels will appear in the modal whenever a member adds or updates credit card information through the member dashboard. Enabling the “Use AVS Billing Address Fields” Setting By default, when trying to update an existing credit card for a member, the available fields are limited to the Card Owner Name and Card Number: When the Use AVS Billing Address Fields advanced setting is enabled: Additional location fields will be added to the same form. This would also apply if the member is updating their credit card via their member dashboard: Keep in mind that when the " Use AVS Billing Address Fields " advanced setting is turned on, the billing address fields on the checkout pages will become mandatory.

title: Edit 404 Error Pages
content: Edit 404 Error Pages Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000012124 When a requested URL does not correspond to an existing page on the website, the server returns a “404 Not Found” error, indicating that the page cannot be located. Common triggers for this error include: A visitor clicks a link on another site that leads to a non-existent page on the directory. A URL that previously existed has been deleted or moved. A visitor mistypes a URL. A bot or crawler (such as from Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, etc.) attempts to access a URL in error. When any of these events occur, the website responds with the 404 error code and displays a designated “404 error page” (the content served when the page cannot be found). How to Create a Custom 404 Page Navigate to My Content >> New Web Page Add a unique Permalink (e.g., "my404") Set the page type as “ Single Web Page ”. Save the page. Once created, the 404 page can be styled and populated with whatever content and links are appropriate for the site. Alternatively, ask the BD Butler to create a unique 404 page design. Selecting the Default 404 Error Page Within the platform’s advanced settings, there is an option labelled Default 404 Error Page . Using the dropdown menu, select the newly created web page (or any existing page) to serve as the designated 404 error page. Default 404 Error Page error_404 How Does a Brilliant Directories Website Handle 404 Error Pages? Historically, all Brilliant Directories-powered websites used the homepage as the 404 error page. While using the homepage can work for human visitors (because they can potentially find their destination via the homepage), the homepage is typically one of the heaviest pages in terms of bandwidth—often loading multiple megabytes. When non-human traffic (such as bots or crawlers) triggers 404 errors and is served the homepage each time, this can consume excessive bandwidth and server resources. To mitigate this, the system now uses a minimal default 404 error page that: Presents a simple notification that the requested page cannot be found. Includes a link to the homepage for genuine users who may wish to continue browsing. Uses significantly less bandwidth (on the order of ~1 KB) compared to loading the full homepage. This change helps reduce unnecessary server load arising from erroneous URL requests while still providing a user-friendly experience for legitimate visitors.

title: Member Signups - Errors and Notifications
content: Member Signups - Errors and Notifications Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000013336 This article explains what the system does when a member tries to sign up for a Free or Paid Membership Plan but for various reason, the system does not allow listing creation.. Paid Membership Plans If a person enters incorrect credit card information on the paid signup form, the payment will be rejected by the payment gateway and an error message displaying the payment gateway response will appear: The visitor will then have the opportunity to update their credit card information and try submitting the form again. In the past, the system created the member and the account was marked as past due. However, now, the member's account will not be created until the payment is completed. Admin Notifications The system will track the failed sign-ups in the Activity Tracker. 1. Find these and other billing-related log entries by navigating to Dashboard » Activity Tracker. 2. TThen go to the Filters section. 3. Filter the results by " Finance ". 4. The category of these messages will be " Failed Transaction ". 5. The description will show the signup details such as the name on the card, email, membership plan, billing cycle, and address. 6. The 'Failed Signup Reason' will appear at the bottom.. This is the most important part of the message because it shows the exact reason the payment failed. The system will also send an email notification of the failed sign-up to the Default Website Email: The system will only send these email notifications when there is a failed paid signup attempt.. If they tried to sign up for a free membership, then no notification will be sent. It is recommended to contact the member by email if the signup was unsuccessful.  This will give the admin an opportunity to offer assistance with the signup process. Note: The system does not consider blocked words added into the "Block Spam Keywords" add-on. This add-on only applies to free membership signup forms.. Free Membership Plans There are different reasons why a free member cannot sign up on the website. For example, if they enter a word added to the 'Block Spam Keywords' list: The system won't allow the member to create an account because the submission will be identified as spam: The error will be displayed in the Dashboard » Activity Tracker. In this case, the error was caused by a blocked spam word, so the exact word will be displayed in the description: There are other errors that may prevent account creation. So It is recommended to review the 'Failed Signup Reason' as it will explain the exact cause of the issue. For more information about the signup process from the member's perspective, please see this article: Member Signups from the Member's Perspective .

title: How Bandwidth and Storage Usage Is Calculated
content: How Bandwidth and Storage Usage Is Calculated Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000013438 In the Dashboard Area of every Brilliant Directories website, there is an indication of the storage that is currently being used and the bandwidth that has been used for the current calendar month: Our server network utilizes the CentOS / WHM / cPanel stack to manage hosting accounts and calculate bandwidth and storage usage data. To measure bandwidth, cPanel & WHM combines the amount of bytes of an incoming data request with the outgoing transferred data (the response to that request). cPanel & WHM obtains this data from the Apache logs. These logs include the following amounts of bandwidth: The total bandwidth that the incoming request that solicited the content used. The total bandwidth that the complete response used (the sum of the size of the content plus the header). For more information about how bandwidth usage data is calculated, and why it may differ from data obtained using other tools, please see the full documentation on this topic here: Apparent Discrepancies in Bandwidth Usage Statistics

title: How To Enable Hotlink Protection
content: How To Enable Hotlink Protection Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000013802 Understanding Hotlink Protection Hotlinking occurs when another website displays files that are hosted on your website, such as images, by directly linking to their source URL. While the content appears on the third-party website, the files are still being served from your website, which means your website's bandwidth and server resources are being used to deliver that content. How Hotlink Protection Works Hotlink protection prevents other websites from directly embedding and displaying files hosted on your website. When enabled, requests originating from unauthorized domains will be blocked from accessing protected content. This can help reduce unnecessary bandwidth usage and prevent third-party websites from using your hosted images and files without permission. Important Considerations Before enabling hotlink protection, keep in mind that some websites and services may no longer be able to display your images if they rely on direct file access. Many major platforms, including social media networks, use their own methods to preview and cache content, so they are generally not affected. However, smaller websites and applications that directly reference your image URLs may be unable to display those files once hotlink protection is enabled. Option 1: Enable Hotlink Protection with Cloudflare If your website is connected to Cloudflare, you can enable Cloudflare's built-in Hotlink Protection feature. Cloudflare Documentation: https://support.cloudflare.com/hc/en-us/articles/200170026-Understanding-Cloudflare-Hotlink-Protection Option 2: Configure Hotlink Protection with an .htaccess File For websites hosted on servers that support Apache configuration files, hotlink protection can also be implemented using rules added to the website's .htaccess file. Reference Guide: https://mediatemple.net/community/products/dv/204644230/prevent-hotlinking-with-a-.htaccess-file Additional Notes Brilliant Directories does not currently include a built-in hotlink protection setting. If hotlink protection is required, it will need to be configured through a service such as Cloudflare or by implementing server-level rules where supported.

title: Manage Your Website's Email Accounts With Microsoft 365
content: Manage Your Website's Email Accounts With Microsoft 365 Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000014019 Manage a Website's Email Accounts with Microsoft 365 Microsoft 365 can host email for a domain connected to a Brilliant Directories website. Microsoft supplies the DNS records that verify the domain and route mail to its service. 1. Add and Verify the Domain in Microsoft 365 Open Settings > Domains in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Add the root domain without www . Copy the TXT verification record supplied by Microsoft. Add that record wherever the domain's live DNS is managed, then complete Microsoft's verification. Microsoft references: Add a custom domain and add DNS records at a DNS provider . 2. Find Where DNS Is Managed If the domain uses Brilliant Directories-managed DNS, open Settings > Domain Manager . Hosted email routing is available under Mailboxes ; see Manage Mailboxes and Email Routing . DNS records can also be managed through Developer Hub > cPanel Dashboard > Zone Editor when that option is available. If the domain uses Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Namecheap, or another provider's nameservers, add the Microsoft records at that provider. Records added in cPanel do not affect a domain whose live DNS is hosted elsewhere. 3. Add the Microsoft 365 Records Copy the exact values from the Microsoft 365 admin center. Common records include: Type Common host Purpose TXT @ or root Verifies domain ownership. MX @ or root Routes incoming mail to Microsoft 365. CNAME autodiscover Helps Outlook locate mailbox settings. TXT @ or root Authorizes Microsoft 365 in SPF. Microsoft can also require CNAME or SRV records for Teams, device enrollment, and other services. Add only the records displayed for the domain and enabled services. See Microsoft's external DNS record reference . 4. Change Mail Routing Create the Microsoft 365 mailboxes before changing MX. Replace obsolete MX records with the Microsoft value and priority shown in the admin center. Leaving conflicting MX records can split or misdirect incoming mail. Microsoft 365 requires the exact mail server hostname supplied in its admin center. Opening this form does not change routing. 5. Configure SPF A domain should publish one SPF TXT record. If SPF already exists, merge the required authorized senders into that record instead of adding a second SPF record. Follow Microsoft's SPF guidance . 6. Verify and Test Use Microsoft's record check, then test sending and receiving. If verification fails, confirm the host/name, destination, priority, spaces, duplicate SPF records, old MX records, and the authoritative DNS provider. Service Boundaries Microsoft manages its mailboxes, billing, passwords, and account access. Brilliant Directories provides DNS or routing controls only when the domain uses supported Brilliant Directories-managed services.

title: Setting Up How Member Reviews Are Approved On The Website
content: Setting Up How Member Reviews Are Approved On The Website Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000014153 To configure how member reviews are approved on your website, go to: Finance » Membership Plans » Profile Page Tab . The review approval workflow is controlled by two settings: Require All Reviews To Be Approved by Admin First – Determines whether an administrator must review and approve new reviews before they can be published. Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member) – Determines whether members can approve or reject reviews submitted to their profile. The combination of these two settings determines how every new review is processed. The four possible workflows are explained below. The combination of these two settings determines how every new review is processed. The four possible workflows are explained below. Scenario 1 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO NO Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO NO By setting both to "NO", all member reviews that are submitted to the website will automatically get published and appear live on the member's profile page and the homepage if the latest reviews are streamed. Scenario 2 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO NO Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO YES Scenario 2 automatically sets all reviews to "WAITING FOR MEMBER". The review will not be published on the website until the member approves the review. The member will also receive an automated notification that there is a pending review in their account. Scenario 3 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO YES Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO YES The third scenario automatically sets all reviews to "WAITING FOR ADMIN". The admin gets an email notification that a review was submitted and must go to the admin area of the website to approve the review manually. » Approving Member Reviews from the Admin Scenario 4 Require All Reviews To be Approved by Admin First: SET TO YES Ability to Accept and Delete Reviews (Member): SET TO NO Our last scenario automatically sets reviews to "WAITING FOR ADMIN". Since members are not able to accept or delete reviews, the admin only has the choice to accept or delete the review. There is no option to notify the member or set it to "WAITING FOR MEMBER". The ADMIN will see the following pop-up when the setting is changed to "APPROVED" » Approving Member Reviews from the Admin Email Templates Linked To New Review Module Depending on your review approval settings, different email templates may be sent to the reviewer or the site administrator. These templates can be customized under Emails → Email Templates . admin-review-notification update-pending-reviews

title: Toolbox » Sidebar Applications
content: Toolbox » Sidebar Applications Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000018932 What is a Sidebar A sidebar is a container that holds widgets, typically displayed to the side of web pages. Common examples of widgets placed in sidebars include banner ads, search modules, and newsletter signup modules. The Brilliant Directories platform comes with a set of predefined sidebars that can be modified and updated according to the website's needs. Sidebar Examples Post Details Pages: Static Pages: Member Search Results: Additional Information: Sidebar Setup Steps For Membership Features/ Post Types How To Add A Sidebar To A Static Page How To Create A Sidebar This is IMPORTANT INFORMATION about Sidebars: Sidebars are containers, not positioning tools. A sidebar simply wraps around a group of widgets that will be used together. Despite the name, a sidebar does not place its widgets on the left or right side of a page; that placement comes from CSS applied on the page where the sidebar is used. Any sidebar can be called with a shortcode. To use a sidebar on a static page, or on any page that does not offer a built-in sidebar option (as the membership features do), add the shortcode with the sidebar's name. For example, for a sidebar named myCustomSidebar, add [ sidebar = name_sidebar ] to the page, placing the code closest to where the sidebar should appear. If needed, style it with CSS to look correct or to mimic a sidebar on a different page. The same sidebar can look different on different pages. Because sidebars carry no positioning CSS of their own, using a sidebar on one page does not guarantee it will look the same on another.

Here is an example of what it could look like: Click on "Save Changes" How To Place Banners On The Website Once the banners are all set, see how to place them on the site by just following these easy instructions: Adding Banners to Sidebars Each Banner that is found in the Banner Ad Design section has its own unique widget name. Adding Banner Ad To Header Adding a banner to the Header requires hiding the search bar that comes by default in the header as there is not enough room for both the banner ad and the search bar. To add both this would be customization and would require that request to go to the marketplace. To add a Banner to the Header please follow these instructions: Upload the image banner or paste the embed code inside the Header Banner design box: Click on "save changes" Go to SETTINGS >> DESIGN SETTINGS >> GENERAL  >> HEADER DESIGN In the "Header Search Module" dropdown select the "Display Header Banner Ad" option: Click "Save Changes" The Header Ad should not be displayed in the Header. This is how the Header Banner Ad will display on the front-end: Adding Below Header Banner Ad This banner can be added under Banner Ads directly: This banner, by default, will display on any pages under the Header besides the homepage (/home) and join page (/join): To allow this banner to display in the Homepage, check the Display on Homepage option: Photo Albums Banner Ad This banner is going to display at the end of the Photo Gallery of a Membership Feature that is using a Photo Gallery, for example, Photo Albums, Products, Properties, and Classifieds. title: "Publish Date" Functionality For The  Admin Blog
content: "Publish Date" Functionality For The  Admin Blog Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019198 What Is A Publish Date? A publish date allows to set a future post date for the admin blog articles. Some users prefer to add multiple articles to their blog in one session, but do not want the articles to get published at the same time, nor do they want to log back in to "Publish" an article and make it live on their website. With the "Publish Date" functionality website admins can now set the date they wish articles to be published on their website. Important: This functionality is exclusively supported for the "Admin Blog" feature (the feature which uses the "Feature - Blog Articles" form). The primary reason this is not available to the member blog feature is that members would be able to cheat the system and re-publish articles allowing their articles to always show first on the website. How To Set A Future Publish Date For An Admin Blog Post To set a future publish date for the admin blog articles please follow these instructions: Go to My Members - Search Members "Login" as the admin blog contributor or whichever member has access to the "Blog" post type Click on "Add Blog Article" Set the article to "Publish" - "Yes". Remember, if the blog has been set to a future publish date, the article will not go live until the publish date. To set a Publish Date click on the "Publish Date" field to open up the calendar. Select the desired date to have the article published on the website: Add the content of the article Click on "Save Changes" How Does The System Allow The Publish Date To Work With The Blog Feature? The "Publish" functionality works exclusively with the "Blog" feature. The system uses the same variable as "events" and "classifieds". All three forms use "post_status", however the functionality is quite different. For "Events" and "Classifieds", the "post_status" variable will publish the post on the website immediately regardless of the date selected.
