title: How to Connect a Domain to a Brilliant Directories Website
content: How to Connect a Domain to a Brilliant Directories Website Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019271 Connect a custom domain, a subdomain, or a free directoryup.com address from Settings > Domain Manager . The connection flow checks the proposed address and shows the pointing instructions before changing the website address. Example on a free directoryup.com address. Additional tabs appear when a custom domain and its services are available. About the examples: The screenshots use Brilliant Directories test websites. demotailwind.com is managed in Cloudflare and illustrates the Cloudflare route; selfautomated.com uses Brilliant Directories nameservers and illustrates the non-Cloudflare alternative. These are alternative DNS arrangements, not consecutive changes to the same domain. Before starting For a custom domain, have access to its DNS provider and registrar. Record the existing mail provider and preserve its MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and other required records. For a Cloudflare connection, have permission to authorize the correct account and domain. For an existing live site, complete the domain-change checklist . Managed SSL installation requires the Managed SSL add-on to be active. A domain change alone does not add that entitlement. Choose the correct site before starting. The final switch changes the website address. The former address is no longer the site’s primary address, and an old-domain redirect must be arranged separately if needed. The wizard has four stages, shown across the top: Choose An Address , Check It , Point Domain , and Switch Over . A completed stage can be clicked to return to it until the switch has run. 1. Choose An Address Open Settings > Domain Manager > Domain . Click Connect my domain name or Change my domain name . Select the appropriate option below. Use a domain from my Cloudflare account : when available, authorize Cloudflare and select a domain from the account. The screen marks this option Fastest — nothing to type . A domain name I own : enter a registered domain or a true subdomain and configure its DNS. A free address from us : choose the portion before .directoryup.com . Choose the route that matches the domain and DNS provider. 2. Check It Enter the address without http:// , https:// , or a page path. A root domain can be typed with or without www., as example.com or www.example.com . The wizard always connects a root domain as www.example.com . A true subdomain is entered exactly, such as members.example.com . If www. is typed in front of a subdomain, the wizard removes it and checks the subdomain itself. For a root domain, choose how the address appears under How should your address appear? : With www. or Without www. . The choice appears as soon as a root domain is typed, and its default follows what was typed. Visitors who type the other version are sent to the chosen one. Without www. needs the root domain itself to point at the website; see Point the root domain . Click Check this address . The box turns green when the address can be checked. A domain extension that does not exist, such as .come , is refused with a message naming it. Resolve any validation message before continuing. For a free address, enter only the chosen prefix using letters, numbers, and hyphens. For Cloudflare, select the intended domain from the account's domain list; use its filter to locate the correct domain. The A domain name I own route: a root domain is typed and the With www. / Without www. choice appears under the box. The Cloudflare route selects the domain from a list instead, as shown below. 3. Point Domain The Point Domain stage reports where the address currently points, names the company where the records are added (the domain's DNS provider, or the registrar when no DNS provider is identified), and lists each record with its own Pointed or Not pointed yet status. Copy the site's own target from this screen; an example address from documentation is not a usable target. Instructions opens the step-by-step guide below the records, and Use a different address returns to Check It . Add the records at the current DNS provider Open the DNS provider's record editor. Add or update the record for the exact host shown in the wizard. Save the DNS change at the provider. Return to Domain Manager. Click Check again . The www record has these fields: Type: CNAME Name: www Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target copied from Domain Manager For a subdomain such as members.example.com , the only record is a CNAME whose name is normally members at the DNS provider, pointing to the same target. The root domain is not changed. For a root domain, the stage lists a second entry for example.com itself: a record, or a forwarding setting on GoDaddy with With www. . With With www. , that entry sends visitors who type example.com on to www.example.com; the website works at www.example.com without it, so Continue is offered once the www record is pointed. With Without www. , example.com is the main address and must reach the website. The root domain cannot take an ordinary CNAME, so the right record depends on the DNS provider; see Point the root domain . The Point Domain stage for a subdomain of a domain in the connected Cloudflare account. Use the target shown by the website being connected. Point the root domain (CNAME exception) DNS does not allow an ordinary CNAME record on the root of a domain (the record named @ ), so the root domain is connected differently depending on the company that runs the domain's DNS. The Point Domain stage identifies that company from the domain's nameservers and shows the matching method below: a CNAME on Cloudflare, Domain Forwarding on GoDaddy when the address uses www, an ALIAS record on Namecheap, and an A record for any other DNS provider or when the provider cannot be identified. An A record works everywhere, but it points at a fixed server address; the Cloudflare, GoDaddy, and Namecheap methods keep the domain following the website if it moves to a different server. Brilliant Directories nameservers Nothing needs to be added. The Point Domain stage reports We manage the DNS for the address, and the records are created during the switch. Cloudflare Cloudflare flattens a CNAME on the root, so the root takes the same record as www. Delete the existing root and www records first, then add both of these: Type: CNAME Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target Type: CNAME Name: www Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target When the Cloudflare account is connected to Domain Manager, Use a domain from my Cloudflare account or Add this record for me creates these records automatically. GoDaddy GoDaddy does not allow a CNAME record on the root of a domain. With With www. , connect it in two steps: Edit the existing www record so it is a CNAME pointing to the site's unique directoryup.com target. Turn on Domain Forwarding so example.com forwards to https://www.example.com : in GoDaddy's DNS settings for the domain, open Forwarding , click Add Forwarding , choose https:// , enter www.example.com , select Permanent (301) , and click Save . GoDaddy's Forwarding settings: forward the root domain to the https www address, permanently (301). The Point Domain stage shows this forwarding in place of a root record, with a link to GoDaddy's guide. Once example.com forwards permanently (301) to https://www.example.com, the root domain reads Pointed on the Point Domain and Switch Over stages. With Without www. , do not turn on Domain Forwarding for the root domain: the website already sends www visitors to example.com, so a forward the other way sends visitors in a circle and the site stops loading. Add an A record for the root instead, alongside the www CNAME: Type: A Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The server address shown for the root domain on the Point Domain stage An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update. Namecheap Namecheap supports an ALIAS record on the root of a domain. Namecheap does not allow an ALIAS record alongside an existing A, AAAA, CNAME, or redirect record for the same host, so delete the current root domain record first, then use Add New Record to create: Type: ALIAS Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target Type: CNAME Name: www Value: The site's unique directoryup.com target Namecheap's guide: How to create an ALIAS record . Other DNS providers Add the www CNAME above, and an A record for the root domain: Type: A Name: @ (the root domain, example.com) Value: The server address shown for the root domain on the Point Domain stage An A record points at a fixed address, so if the website moves to a different server in the future, that one record needs the same update. For the long term, moving the domain's DNS to a free Cloudflare account avoids this, because Cloudflare can hold the site's target on the root domain; see Connecting a Site to Cloudflare . Use a connected Cloudflare account After Cloudflare authorization, filter the domain list and select the intended domain. Choose its main www. address or enter a subdomain, then click Use this address . The wizard prepares the DNS records and advances to Switch Over , skipping the Point Domain stage. To see the record it added, click Show me the DNS record you added on the Switch Over stage. Start over returns to the three choices. A domain entered through A domain name I own can also be on Cloudflare. When the domain is in the Cloudflare zone already connected to the site, the Point Domain stage offers Add this record for me . When it is on Cloudflare under a different zone or account, the stage offers Set it up for me , or Sign in and set it up for me when the account holding that domain is not connected yet. Use the offered button, or expand I would rather add the record myself to add the record by hand, then click Check again . Preparing a record does not complete the website-address switch; the final confirmation is still required. See Cloudflare in Domain Manager . Filter the Cloudflare domain list, select the intended domain, and choose the main address or a subdomain. Move the entire domain's DNS to Brilliant Directories The nameserver alternative is appropriate when the whole domain's DNS should be managed by Brilliant Directories. It is not necessary merely to connect one subdomain. On the Point Domain stage, select Nameservers instead of DNS record to show the two nameservers, then replace the domain's nameservers at the registrar with both of them: Nameserver: ns1.directorysecure.com Nameserver: ns2.directorysecure.com When the domain already uses these nameservers, the Point Domain stage reports We manage the DNS for the address. There is nothing to add; the record is created during the switch. A nameserver change can take a few hours to reach everyone. A nameserver change affects the whole domain. The wizard warns that this moves all DNS to Brilliant Directories. Preserve and recreate the records required by existing email and other services before changing nameservers. For a single subdomain while the main website or email stays elsewhere, use the subdomain CNAME route. Free directoryup.com addresses do not need records changed at an external registrar; their flow skips the Point Domain stage. Non-Cloudflare example: selfautomated.com is registered at GoDaddy and uses Brilliant Directories nameservers. The Domain tab confirms that both the main address and the address without www are connected. 4. Switch Over Click Continue after reviewing the pointing result. When the main address is not pointed yet, this button reads Continue anyway . Check Now and After the change . After the change lists the main address first and, for a root domain, the other version with forwards to . Each shows its own status: Pointed , Cannot verify , Checking… , or Not pointed yet . Click Not pointed yet to see what is missing; Show me what to set up returns to Point Domain . Read the message above the buttons. Ready to switch to the new address appears when it is ready; otherwise What happens when you switch describes the change. Both name the current address, which stops loading the website once the switch is done. Click Switch to this address . Confirm Yes, switch it in the confirmation dialog. Keep the page open until the progress screen completes. Do not treat a Not pointed yet result as a completed connection. Continue anyway allows the switch before DNS is ready: the new address does not load the website until its record is in place, and the current address stops working straight away. If Without www. was chosen but the root domain does not reach the website yet, the switch keeps the website on the www version and Domain Manager says so. Change it later under Web address style once the root domain points at the website; see Set Up The WWW or Non-WWW Version Of The Domain . Review the current and new addresses and the message above the buttons before confirming the switch. Confirm the result The completion screen identifies the new address and the remaining setup tasks. Email authentication is attempted during the switch when the connected DNS service can accept the records. If manual setup is required, follow the Emails tab's instructions. Managed SSL installation is attempted when the add-on is active; certificate issuance can finish after the address change. The switch also moves the website's sending address to the new domain when it used the old domain or a placeholder address, keeping the part before the @. An address at another domain, such as a Gmail address, is left unchanged. The completed switch identifies the new address and the remaining SSL and integration tasks. Website sender authentication is separate from incoming-mail setup. Open the new website address. Review the SSL tab. Review Emails > Sender Authentication . Test website forms, login, and any domain-restricted integrations. DNS changes can take time to become visible everywhere. Use Check again and compare the exact host and target if the connection remains unresolved. Contact support with the domain, site ID, and displayed error when the records appear correct but the site still fails. Free-address testing has separate limitations; see directoryup.com Subdomain Test Credentials .

title: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover
content: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019275 IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless the site has heavy customizations to the underlying code of the website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use around the website. This article will cover the image settings for the following: Profile Photo for Website Profile Photo for Social Media Sharing Profile Logo for Website Profile Logo for Social Media Sharing Profile Cover On the Image Settings page, these settings are in the Member Photos , Member Logos and Cover Photos sections, listed under Image Sizes in the side menu. Changes on the Image Settings page take effect only after Save is clicked in the save bar at the top of the page. 1 — the Member Photos, Member Logos and Cover Photos sections in the side menu. 2 — the settings of the selected section. Additional Information: Image Settings - Member Post Types- Single Photo Image Settings - Member Post Types - Multiple Photos Profile Logo Settings Here are some things to know regarding editing Profile Logo: The profile logo can be set to either an “Open” ratio or a fixed aspect ratio of 3:4 or 1:1 . More details on how aspect ratios work can be found here. When selecting the “Open” option, members are not restricted to a specific shape. This means they can upload images that are square, wider than they are tall, or taller than they are wide. With the ratio set to “Open” , the Width and Height values act as maximum limits rather than fixed dimensions. For example, if both values are set to 200px and a member uploads a 2000px × 2000px image, the system will automatically resize it to 200px × 200px . The image’s original proportions are preserved, but it is scaled down so it does not exceed the defined limits. This resizing helps ensure that images remain optimized for performance, allowing pages to load faster and improving the overall browsing experience across the website. 1 — the Profile Logo setting. 2 — its Ratio, which can be Open, 1:1 or 3:4. Entering a "Profile Logo" width of less than 162px shows a Warning message, and the width is reset to 162px: *This is done to make sure that large images are resized to dimensions that will look relatively uniform in the various areas of the website where profile logos are used. Entering a "Profile Logo Social Media" width or height of less than the required 200px shows a Warning message, and the value is reset to 200px: Profile Photo Settings The Profile Photo Settings function much like the Profile Logo Settings, with one key difference; Profile Photos allow you to set an aspect ratio of 3:4 or 1:1. This helps ensure that profile images fit properly across different areas of the website where they are displayed. Please note: Changing the default Aspect Ratios is possible, but not recommended.  Doing so would require customizing the design of the website significantly in order to accommodate a different aspect ratio for these images around the website and should only be requested by Advanced Users of the software that have significant experience in customizing the design of Brilliant Directories websites. Profile Cover Settings Here are some things to know regarding editing Profile Cover: The ratio of the Profile Cover will always be "Open" so members are not forced to upload an image that is a certain shape - wider than it is tall, or taller than it is wide. Since the ratio is always "Open", the "Width" and "Height" numbers serve as limits for the maximum width and height of the image.  For example, if the Width and height are set to 1200px x 500px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 800px tall, the final image will be resized to be 1 200px wide x 500px tall, maintaining the same aspect ratio of the original image, but downsizing it to be no more than the limit.  This helps ensure that the website loads these images as quickly and efficiently as possible, thus reducing the overall time to load all of the website's pages as much as possible. How To Upload Logo Images As A Member Login as a member and go to the "Profile Photo" Tab Click on "Upload Logo" (once a logo has been uploaded, the button reads "Change Logo"): NOTE: Accepted Image formats are: JPG, PNG, GIF and WEBP 3. Click "Choose Logo" and select an image to upload. It opens in the cropping window: 4. Click "Click to Save Photo". If the logo is not large enough the member will receive the following message, warning them that the current image is smaller than 200px x 200px and will have to be stretched in order to meet the minimum size requirements for sharing on social media websites, and the logo will appear on the website at a smaller size than other Profile Logos. This warning appears only when the Skip Image Size Warning for Profile Photos and Logos Advanced Setting (system variable skip_photo_upload_warning_size) is turned off. It is ON by default, so by default the image is uploaded without the warning. How To Upload Profile Photos As A Member When uploading the profile photo, they will follow the same process as uploading a Profile Logo.  However, the members will be required to use the built-in cropping tool which will ensure that the final image uses the 3:4 Aspect Ratio specified in the Profile Photo Settings: If the photo is smaller than 200px x 200px, clicking "Click to Save Photo" shows the following warning, and "Upload and Stretch" uploads it anyway. This warning appears only when the Skip Image Size Warning for Profile Photos and Logos Advanced Setting (system variable skip_photo_upload_warning_size) is turned off. It is ON by default, so by default the image is uploaded without the warning. It is now possible to zoom in & out , rotate , and flip profile photo images while cropping, using the tools below the image: How To Upload Cover Images As A Member When uploading the cover photo, they will follow the same process as uploading a Profile Picture/Logo. However, the members will be required to use the built-in cropping tool which will ensure that the final image uses the dimensions specified in the Profile Cover Settings : Additional Information The image module is made up of text labels that can be edited: » How to locate Text Labels on the Front end of a Website » Settings » Text Labels

title: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Single Photo
content: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Single Photo Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019276 IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless doing heavy customizations to the underlying code of a website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use on a Brilliant Directories website. This article will cover the image settings for the following: Single Photo Post - Thumbnail Single Photo Post - Large On the Image Settings page, these settings are in the Single Photo Posts section, listed under Image Sizes in the side menu. Changes on the Image Settings page take effect only after Save is clicked in the save bar at the top of the page. 1 — Single Photo Posts in the side menu. 2 — the Single Photo Post - Thumbnail and Single Photo Post - Large settings. We also have the following articles available that cover the other sections: Image Settings - Profile Photos & Logos Image Settings - Member Post Types - Multiple Photos Default Member Post Types That These Settings Apply To These settings apply to all member post types where one photo can be added to a single post.  These post types include: Member Article Blog Article Event Coupon Jobs Single Photo Post - Thumbnail Settings This setting determines the maximum dimensions that single-photo member post type will have when viewed in most locations around the website (homepage streaming widgets, member profile pages, and search results).  The only place this setting does not apply is the Details page of the post (the single page devoted to the full post) .  The setting for the size of the photo on the Details page of the post is set by the " Single Photo Post - Large" setting (see section below). The recommended default settings are a free (open) ratio, a width of 272, and a height of 160. The ratio of the Single Photo Post - Thumbnail will always be "Open" so members are not forced to upload an image that is a certain shape - it can be square, wider than it is tall, or taller than it is wide. Since the ratio is always "Open", the "Width" and "Height" numbers serve as limits for the maximum width and height of the image.  For example, if both the Width and Height are set to 200px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 2000px tall, the final image will be resized to be 200px wide x 200px tall, maintaining the same aspect ratio of the original image, but downsizing it to be no more than the 200px x 200px limit. This helps ensure that the website loads these images as quickly and efficiently as possible, thus reducing the overall time to load all of the website's pages as much as possible. As another example, if both the Width and height are set to 200px, and a member uploads an image that is 2000px wide x 1000px tall, the image will be resized so that it fits within the limits of 200px x 200px, without changing the aspect ratio.  In this example, the final uploaded image would be 200px wide x 100px tall so it fits within the 200px x 200px limit without changing its aspect ratio or stretching / distorting the image. If the "Single Photo Post - Thumbnail" width is set to less than 160px, a Warning message appears and the width is reset to 160px: ** This is done to make sure that large images are resized to dimensions that will look relatively uniform in the various areas of the website where single photo member post type thumbnails are used. Even though images can be set to be smaller than the default settings, we do not recommend doing so unless customizing the underlying code of the website's design to accommodate these smaller images. The Width and Height settings can be set as high as needed, but please note doing this will not cause the images to DISPLAY larger around the site,  The image itself will be saved at a larger size, but will be shrunk down to fit into the space available for it when displayed on the website.  In other words, all of the images will take longer and use more bandwidth to load, and will not display any larger on the website.  Making these images larger will only be useful if  heavily customizing the underlying code of the website's design to accommodate these larger images. Single Photo Post - Large Settings This setting determines the maximum dimensions that single-photo member posts type will have when viewed on the Details page of the post (the single page devoted to the full post). The recommended default settings are a free (open) ratio, a width of 375, and a height of 375.  This is also the image used when sharing the Details page of the post on social media. A single image post will have the Image Upload field directly on the form: Recommended Size : 750 by 400 pixels The recommended size text is a text label. System Variable : recommended_size_single_photo The articles below will explain how to upload these types of posts: » How to Post an Event » How to Post a Coupon » How to Post a Community Article » How to Post a Job Offer

title: Developer Hub » Image Settings
content: Developer Hub » Image Settings Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019278 What are the Image Settings? The Image Settings of the website determine the final size that images will be saved after being uploaded to the website by members. The default settings that come with a Brilliant Directories website are designed so that images will fit well in all of the areas of the website in which they display while being optimized for load speed and meeting minimum requirements for social media sharing. IMPORTANT NOTE: Unless doing heavy customizations to the underlying code of the website's design, there is no need to touch these settings as they will already be optimized for use on a Brilliant Directories website. How to Access the Image Settings Go to ADMIN » DEVELOPER HUB and click Edit Image Sizes on the Image Settings card: Using the Image Settings Page The page lists every image size in one place, grouped into sections: Search — type part of a setting's name to show only the matching settings. The number of results appears below the box, and Clear (or the X in the box) shows every setting again. Side menu — click a section to jump to it. The Image Sizes group holds Member Photos , Member Logos , Cover Photos , Single Photo Posts , Album Posts and Text Editor Images . The Page Speed group holds Lazy Loading . Settings — each section lists its image sizes with a Width and Height in pixels, plus a Ratio for the member photo and logo sizes. Restore Defaults — puts every image size and the lazy loading setting back to the platform defaults (see below). Searching for a setting: Saving Changes Changes on this page are not saved until Save is clicked. As soon as a value changes, the edited setting is marked with a dot and a save bar appears at the top of the page with the message Unsaved changes and two buttons: Save — saves every change on the page at once, including the Lazy Loading setting. The button briefly shows Saved when the save is complete. Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac) does the same while the save bar is showing. Discard — asks Discard Unsaved Changes? and, after Discard Changes is clicked, puts back the values that were last saved. Keep Editing closes the question without losing anything. Changing a size and then discarding the change: Some values are checked as they are entered. A width or height below the minimum allowed for that image (EG 162 pixels for the Profile Logo width) shows a Warning message and the value is reset to the minimum. The articles linked at the end of this page cover the limits for each image size. Restore Defaults Clicking Restore Defaults asks for confirmation first. After Restore Defaults is clicked in the confirmation, every image size goes back to its recommended size and Lazy Load Images goes back to Load Images After Scroll . These values are saved right away , with no separate Save step, and the website uses the new sizes immediately. Click Cancel to leave the settings unchanged. General Image Settings Information Lazy Loading ( Load Images After Scroll / Load Images After Page Load / Disabled ) The Lazy Load Images setting is in the Lazy Loading section, under Page Speed in the side menu. Like every other setting on the page, a new choice takes effect only after Save is clicked in the save bar. 1 — Lazy Loading in the side menu, under Page Speed. 2 — the Lazy Load Images setting. Lazy Loading is a set of techniques in web and application development that defers the loading of resources on a page to a later point in time—when those resources are actually needed instead of loading them upfront. These techniques help in improving performance, better utilization of the device’s resources, and reducing associated costs with bandwidth consumption. Load Images After Scroll: Images will only start loading once the page scrolls showing new data and images (Best bandwidth consumption efficiency) Load Images After Page Load: Once the first images Above the fold are loaded, it starts loading images below the fold (quickly loads pages, but consumes more bandwidth) Best for Carousels and Streaming Widgets. Disabled: Loads all images by default. Ratio The "Ratio" refers to the Aspect Ratio of the image, which is how large the height of an image will be relative to the width of the image and vice-versa. For example, a 1:1 aspect ratio means it will be a square - for every 1 pixel of width, the image will have 1 pixel of height. As another example, the Aspect Ratio of an HD television is 16:9 (a rectangle that is wider than it is tall), meaning the image on the television will have 16 pixels of width for every 9 pixels of height. An "Open" aspect ratio means there is no set aspect ratio at all, meaning the image can be any shape. For more information about Aspect Ratios, please see the Wikipedia article on the topic . Width The maximum width of the final image in pixels. Height The maximum height of the final image in pixels. Social Media Sharing When uploading an image, two copies of the image will be saved: one that is optimized for display on the website, and one that is optimized for social media sharing. Currently, Facebook and many other popular social media sites require images to be at least 200px x 200px to be shared on their platform. One copy of the image will be saved to be at least this size, and another will be saved that is optimized for displaying on the website where a smaller size is required. Adding Images for Members Users can upload Logos and Profile Photos through the member dashboard: How to Complete a Profile as a Member Admins can import members with Logos and Profile Photos through the import file: Importing Members with Images These images are added as links into an import file that is uploaded and then added to the corresponding member profile. Using links to add member Logos and Profile Photos is only available through the member import file. Specific Image Settings Information For more information about the settings available on this page as they apply to different areas of the site, check out the following articles: Developer Hub » Image Settings » Profile Photos, Logos & Cover Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Single Photo Developer Hub » Image Settings » Member Post Types - Multiple Photos Developer Hub » Image Settings » Froala Text Editor Images

title: FROALA Text Editor: Versions and their Upload Functionalities
content: FROALA Text Editor: Versions and their Upload Functionalities Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019667 When creating a post, such as a blog article, there is a Froala Text Editor which allows modifying styles such as the font size, font colors, boldness, and more. There are different text editor versions available that either restrict or allow for image upload and video embed. These can be used and applied individually via the FORM MANAGER to the respective forms for the members' "ABOUT ME" section and all post types such as coupons, properties, classifieds, member articles, website blog articles, etc. This form field type is only supported for forms used within the Member Dashboard. This provides the ability to control if members can add images and video embeds into the text editor input fields of posts and their "ABOUT ME" section. The Froala Editor currently supports 38 languages , check which languages are supported: https://www.froala.com/wysiwyg-editor/languages. The Froala Editor is going to use the language that is set in the Settings >> General Settings >> Localization tab >> Default Website Language. How To Enable Froala Editors There are three built-in versions of the Froala Text Editor. You can add any of them to a form, and each one controls things like whether users can upload images or embed YouTube videos. For details on where each editor is used throughout the site and what features they include, click the link below: Everything About WYSIWYG Editors Available Text Editors There are Froala Text Editor - Basic No image upload, video embed, or source code editor Basic text editor with limited options to edit font size, colors, styles, and create bullet checklists. The Basic Froala Text Editor includes the following styling options: Bold Italic Underline Font Size Paragraph Format Line Height Text Color Background Color Clear Formatting Ordered List Unordered List Insert Horizontal Line Insert a Link The basic editor only provides basic font formatting. title: How to Add a Facebook Feed to Member Profile Pages
content: How to Add a Facebook Feed to Member Profile Pages Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019740 Business accounts can stream their Facebook feed in the sidebar of their profile. With this functionality, the Facebook Feed streams all of the latest posts and updates from a specific Facebook account. The Facebook Feed will display the posts in chronological order: Important Only Facebook Company Pages or Fan Pages will stream content. The tool only works with public Facebook company pages. If a member uses their personal Facebook account link, then the feed will show an error or a blank widget. Facebook does not allow personal Facebook pages from being streamed.* * There is nothing that Brilliant Directories can do to change this limitation imposed by Facebook. Add the Facebook Feed to Member Profile Pages The Facebook Feed widget is found in the Sidebar Manager. Follow the steps below. Go to the Toolbox » Sidebar Manager » Member Profile Page sidebar: Search for " Member Facebook Feed " in the Member Profile Page sidebar. Drag the " Bootstrap Theme - Module - Member Facebook Feed " widget into the display position on the Member Profile Page sidebar: Click on "Save Changes" Please note that a Facebook Feed will only show on a member's profile page if they have added a proper facebook link in their contact details form: Facebook Company Page The tool only works with public Facebook company pages. If a member uses their personal Facebook account link, then the feed will show an error or a blank widget: These Facebook accounts won't work for the Facebook Feed: If it's a personal Facebook profile (not a company page). If it's a company page, but not public (users must be logged into FB to see the timeline) If it's an invalid Facebook Link If the company Facebook page is still not published Is my Facebook account a personal profile or a page? Facebook pages must be public for the feed to work. When not logged in to Facebook the information will be still accessible. For example, our Facebook page is a public page: https://www.facebook.com/BrilliantDirectories On the other hand, Facebook profiles or private pages are not available unless logged in to the Facebook account, so it will always prompt the user to log in: If a Facebook link asks for login credentials to continue, that link won't work for the Facebook Feed. Difference between Profile and Business Page For more information about the difference between a Facebook profile and a page go to the link below: » https://www.facebook.com/help/337881706729661 Note We updated the Facebook Activity Feed widgets to display the content from this 3rd party site after the rest of the page loads to improve page load times and page speed scores.

title: Guide 9. How to Enable Maps with Google Maps API
content: Guide 9. How to Enable Maps with Google Maps API Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000019818 In order to use location search and Google Maps features on a Brilliant Directories website, a Google Maps API key must be created in Google Cloud and added to the site admin. >> Google Maps API: Features, Functions, and Key Considerations The Google Maps API key is what lets Google Maps work on the website. The key is created in Google Cloud, which is managed by Google, not Brilliant Directories. Because of this, the setup screens may look a little different for each person depending on their Google account, location, billing setup, or whether they have used Google Cloud before. Important Notes The live domain should be connected before completing the Google Maps API setup. For help connecting a live domain, see: How To Move A Site To A Live Domain Google requires billing to be enabled for Google Maps Platform projects. Google controls billing requirements, credits, limits, and account settings. If Google Cloud Console opens a blank screen, redirects unexpectedly, or loses the setup session, return to the Google Maps Platform page and select Get Started again. Most of this setup happens inside Google Cloud. The final step happens inside the Brilliant Directories admin. Step 1 - Create Account Start by opening Google Maps Platform: >> Open Google Maps Platform Click Create an account to get started, or open the Google Cloud Console. Google may ask for account setup, billing information, or project details before continuing. If Google asks setup questions, answer them based on the website or project being connected. These questions are managed by Google and may vary by account. Step 2 - Enable Billing Goal : The Google Cloud project must have billing enabled before Google Maps can work properly on the website. Open the Google Cloud Billing page: Open Google Cloud Billing [WATCH] How to create a billing account Select the same Google Cloud project being used for the website and confirm that billing is active. If billing is not active, follow Google’s prompts to add or connect a billing account. Google Maps Connect Billing If Google rejects the payment method, requires identity verification, or shows a billing account error, that issue must be resolved directly inside Google Cloud. Step 3 - Enable the APIs Goal : Enable the required Google Maps APIs for the same Google Cloud project. Open each API link below and enable it for the Google Cloud project being used for the website. Enable Maps JavaScript API Enable Places API (New) Enable Geocoding API [WATCH] How to enable Google Maps Platform APIs Make sure the correct Google Cloud project is selected at the top of the Google Cloud Console before enabling each API. If Google shows a different screen than expected, focus on the outcome of this step: each of the required APIs should be enabled for the same project. Google Maps Enabling an API Step 4 - Create the API Key Goal : Create one Google Maps API key that will be added to the Brilliant Directories admin. Open the Google Cloud Credentials page: Open Google Cloud Credentials Click Create credentials . Select API key . The Create API key panel opens. The API restrictions (Step 5) and website restrictions (Step 6) can be set here before clicking Create , or added later by editing the key. Copy the new API key. Google may show slightly different labels depending on the account. The main goal is to create an API key inside the same project where the required APIs were enabled. Step 5 - Restrict API Access Goal : Limit the API key so it can only access the Google Maps APIs needed for the website. Open the API key from the Google Cloud Credentials page: Open Google Cloud Credentials In the Create API key panel, or on the Edit API key page of an existing key, find the Select API restrictions list. Open the list, select the APIs used by the website, and click OK : Maps JavaScript API Places API (New) Geocoding API If one of these APIs does not appear in the list, return to Step 3 and confirm that the API was enabled for the same Google Cloud project. When editing an existing key, click Save after selecting the APIs. In the Create API key panel, finish Step 6 first, then click Create . Step 6 - Restrict the API Key Goal : Restrict the API key so it can only be used by the approved website domains. This step is important because it tells Google which websites are allowed to use the API key. Under application restrictions, select: Websites Then click Add under Website restrictions and add the allowed website referrers one at a time. Required Referrers Use the examples below as a guide. Replace example.com with the final domain of the website. *.directoryup.com/* *.managemydirectory.com/* managemydirectory.com *.example.com/* example.com The directoryup.com referrer is useful if the site is not live yet. The managemydirectory.com referrers are needed so map-related features can work properly inside the Brilliant Directories admin area. The custom domain referrers allow the API key to work on the live website domain. Google Maps: Edit HTTP Referrers After adding the referrers, click Create in the Create API key panel, or Save when editing an existing key. Step 7 - Add the API Key Goal : Add the finished Google Maps API key to the Brilliant Directories admin. Go to Settings . Click General Settings . Click the Integrations tab. Paste the Google Maps API key into the Google Maps Javascript API Key field. Click Save Changes . Optional shortcut: type Google Maps in the Search by Keyword box at the top right of General Settings to show only the matching fields. After saving, the Google Maps API key is connected to the website. Step 8 - Check the Result Goal : Confirm that Google accepts the key. Right after Save Changes , the Integrations tab tests the key with Google and shows the result below the key field: Website key : green ( Google Maps key is working or Maps work on your website ) means Google accepts the key. A key restricted to the website's domain is tested on the live domain, the way visitors use it. Server key : the optional server key, used to geocode members during imports. No server key saved in grey is fine for most sites. A red result names the problem. Click it to see the fix steps and edit the key; a key Google refuses there is not saved. For each possible result, see Google Maps Issues: Index . Google API Usage Different Brilliant Directories features may use different Google Maps services. Front-End Website Features Member profile maps: Maps JavaScript API Location searches: Places API (New) and Geocoding API Detect Visitor Location Add-On: Geocoding API Member Dashboard Features Contact details forms: Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), and Geocoding API Post forms with location fields: Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), and Geocoding API Multi-Location Add-On: Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), and Geocoding API Admin Dashboard Features Geocode Members tool: Geocoding API Location searches in admin tools: Places API (New) and Geocoding API Enable All Location Features For Pretty URL Search Results Pages advanced setting: Geocoding API FAQ Google Cloud Screen Does Not Match This Article -- Google may update labels, layouts, and setup screens at any time. If the screen looks different, focus on the goal listed in each step. The main requirements are still the same: billing must be active, the required APIs must be enabled, the API key must be created, and the key must be restricted to the correct website domains. Google Shows a Questionnaire -- The questionnaire is part of Google’s setup process. Answer the questions based on the website or project being connected. Brilliant Directories does not require one specific answer pattern for the Google questionnaire. SDK Options Appear in Google -- For a standard Brilliant Directories website setup, SDK options are not needed. Ignore iOS SDK, Android SDK, Navigation SDK, Fleet Engine, and mobile app setup options unless a separate custom mobile app project specifically requires them. The API Does Not Appear When Restricting the Key -- If Maps JavaScript API, Places API (New), or Geocoding API does not appear in the API restrictions list, the API may not be enabled for the selected Google Cloud project. Return to Step 3, confirm the correct project is selected, and enable the missing API. When to Contact Brilliant Directories Support Contact Brilliant Directories Support if: The API key has been added to the Brilliant Directories admin, but maps are still not loading The correct APIs appear to be enabled, but the website still shows a map error There is uncertainty about where to add the API key inside the Brilliant Directories admin Location features are not working after the Google setup has been completed When to Contact Google Support Some issues must be handled directly inside Google Cloud because Google controls the account, billing, verification, project, and API key system. Contact Google Support or review Google Cloud Help if: Billing cannot be activated Google rejects the payment method The Google Cloud account is locked, suspended, or restricted Google requires identity verification The Google Cloud project cannot be accessed Google shows billing, permissions, or account-level errors

title: Setting Up Locations For UK Directories
content: Setting Up Locations For UK Directories Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000021026 Your Brilliant Directories website is integrated with Google Maps API. This means that your website is powered by the robust functionality of Brilliant Directories. This also means that there are certain limitations regarding what Brilliant Directories can do to edit Google Maps functionality. Here are some important items every United Kingdom Website owner should be aware of: Google Location Types Google assigns "United Kingdom" as the "Country" location type and "England" as the "Administrative Area Level 1" type which is normally reserved for States and Provinces. In all, Brilliant Directories uses five location types that you can set to either "bounds" or "radius". The Bounding and Radius Location Searches articles outlines in detail the difference between these settings and what each means. It is important to understand that although only five settings appear in the admin, there are 24 total location types that are controlled by these six primary settings, and all are based on the Google Location response. The parent settings are: "Zip / Postal Code" searches are for Zip Codes "Locality" searches are for cities "Administrative Area Level 2" searches are for counties "Administrative Area Level 1" searches are for States and Provinces Country There is a sixth location type that the Brilliant Directories system does not provide settings or SEO templates for: "Neighborhood" searches are very rarely used and we would recommend not modifying this setting The following chart shows all of the google location types and which primary setting they are tied to: Click here for complete documentation on the Google Maps Locations Hiding "United Kingdom" From URL Structure Brilliant Directories makes it easy to hide the "country" location type and swamp it for the " Administrative Area Level 1". This means that your member and feature posts URL structure will go from looking like this: http://mysite.com/united-kingdom/medecine/dr-patrick-awesome To http://mysite.com/england/medecine/dr-patrick-awesome To accomplish this, navigate to the Settings >> Advanced Settings and conduct a search for Member Profile URL Structure setting: The next step would be replacing the country_name variable with the state_name variable. After the changes, the new structure would look like this: Optimizing Field Labels via Form Manager To Match United Kingdom Locations IMPORTANT NOTE: Do not edit the "Database Variable" in form of the default fields. Editing this variable name will not return the correct end results. Navigate to Toolbox >> Form Manager and click Customize on a default Contact Details Form: Enable the Display View for the field with the variable name country_code if planning to display this value on profiles pages and disable it this field needs to be hidden on profile pages. Remember that the "Country" value will always be "United Kingdom" hence many site owners choose to hide this: Enable the Display View for the field with the variable name state_code if planning to display this value on profiles pages and disable it this field needs to be hidden on profile pages. Keep in mind that the "State" will always be England, Ireland, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales for UK directories. Optional #1 : If you wish to add neighborhoods such as "Basford" or "Canton", create a new field for this location type. To add a new field, simply click on Add Field button. This is how this newly created field would look like: Optional #2: If you wish to add UK counties such as "Nottinghamshire", create a new field for this location type. To add a new field, simply click on Add Field button. This is how this newly created field would look like: Very Important Note: Keep in mind that the steps Optional #1 and #2 are hard coded solutions that do not integrate with the location database. These custom variables will exist in the database but they will need to be called on the search results via customization. title: Automatic IP Address Blocking - The firewall on this server is blocking your connection
content: Automatic IP Address Blocking - The firewall on this server is blocking your connection Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000021119 Understanding IP Blocks and Site Accessibility The Brilliant Directories platform includes automated security measures to help protect websites from malicious activity. One of these measures is an IP address blocking system, which temporarily restricts access from IPs that exhibit potentially harmful behavior. Important note: when an IP is blocked, the website itself remains online and accessible to all other users — the issue is limited to the specific blocked IP address. This is a screenshot of the firewall message: In approximately 95% of cases, an IP address is blocked because automated systems detect behavior consistent with attempts to exploit vulnerabilities. These blocks are implemented automatically to prevent potential security breaches and to maintain overall server integrity. In about 5% of cases, blocks occur due to false positives — typically triggered by repeated failed login attempts or other unusual access patterns. These are some of the most common triggers: 10 failed login attempts within a 1-hour period 10 failed login attempts to an email account within a 1-hour period 5 failed email sending attempts using the domain name 5 failed login attempts to cPanel within 1 hour 5 failed login attempts via SSH within 1 hour (usually limited to use by developers or server administrators) When a block occurs, the website continues to operate normally for all other users. The block applies only to the specific IP address that triggered the activity threshold. If access is unintentionally restricted, switching to a different network often restores access. Please also contact support@brilliantdirectories.com so that we can help review and resolve the block. These measures are in place to ensure long-term platform reliability and security for all directory websites.

title: Bulk Delete Or Move All Members From A Specific Membership Plan
content: Bulk Delete Or Move All Members From A Specific Membership Plan Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000021382 This article explains how to delete all members from a membership plan or move them to another membership plan. This is a great feature, especially when importing members. It is best practice to import new members into a dedicated, empty membership plan. This ensures that if any issues arise during the import process, the batch can be safely bulk-deleted without affecting existing users. Once the data is verified, these members can easily be transferred to their active membership plans. Deleting Members To delete all members from a specific membership plan, please follow these instructions: Go to Finance » Membership Plans. Click "Actions" and select "Delete": Select one of the following options: - Only delete members from this membership plan. - Delete membership plan and all its members. Click "Yes, Continue". All members in that membership plan will be deleted. Moving Members To move members from one membership plan to another, please follow these instructions: Go to Finance » Membership Plans. Click o "Actions" and select "Move Members": Select the membership plan to which the members will be moved and click "Continue": Click "Yes, Continue": This action moves all members to the new membership plan. However, it is important to note that the system does not automatically create new subscriptions as part of this process. To assign different subscriptions under the new plan, the existing subscriptions must be canceled before new subscriptions are created manually. The steps for creating new subscriptions are outlined in this guide.

title: How To Edit Member Dashboard Forms & Add Custom Fields
content: How To Edit Member Dashboard Forms & Add Custom Fields Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000021796 This article explains how to identify and edit the forms members fill out inside their member dashboard. These forms can be customized by editing existing fields, deleting fields, or adding new custom fields where supported. Identify the Form Being Used Before editing a form, first confirm which form is assigned to the membership plan. Go to: Finance Membership Plans Select the membership plan to edit Open the Member Dashboard tab. This section shows the member dashboard forms enabled for that membership plan. Click Edit Form for the form that needs to be updated. From there, form fields can be added, removed, or edited. Important Notes New custom fields can be added to the Contact Details and Listing Details forms. Existing form fields can be edited or deleted. New fields can technically be added to the About form, but saved information from those fields will not display on the member profile. It is best to finalize form fields before launching the website and before members begin saving profile information. Edit an Existing Form Field In this example, an existing field is edited in the Listing - Contact Details - Member Form . Go to: Toolbox Form Manager Click Customize for the form, or Edit if the form has already been customized Find the field that needs to be updated, make the changes, and click Save Changes . In this example, the Company Name field was changed to Business Name . After the member saves the updated field in the dashboard, the updated label will display on the member profile. Delete an Existing Form Field To delete a field, open the form in the Form Manager and find the field that needs to be removed. Click Delete Field from the Actions dropdown. Important: If a member already saved information in a deleted field, that saved data may still appear on the member profile because it remains stored in the database. For this reason, it is best to finalize form fields before launching the website or before members begin adding profile information. Add a New Form Field In this example, a new field is added to the Listing - Additional Details - Member Form . Go to: Toolbox Form Manager Click Customize for the form, or Edit if the form has already been customized Click Add Field . Enter the field details, including the Field Label and Database Variable . Select the field type and enable Display View if the field should display on the member profile. Once saved, the new field will display in the member dashboard form. After the member saves information in the new field, the field will display on the member profile if Display View is enabled.

title: How to Verify a Listing
content: How to Verify a Listing Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000021982 Overview The Verified Listing feature allows administrators to manually verify member listings. Once verified, a badge appears on the member's public profile, indicating to site visitors that the listing has been reviewed and verified by the site administrator. A default checkmark badge is displayed on verified profiles. When a site visitor hovers over the badge, a message confirms that the listing is verified. ⚠ NOTE — Verification Is Always Manual : The system does not verify members automatically. Regardless of whether a member submits a verification form, the verified status is only applied when an administrator manually sets the member to Verified via the Quick Edit module. The form submission is a request, it does not trigger automatic verification. Part 1 — Enable the Verify Listing Option on a Membership Plan The Verify Listing option must be enabled on a Membership Plan before members on that plan can see or submit a verification request from their dashboard. Navigation Path: Admin Dashboard » Finance » Membership Plans » Member's Dashboard To enable the setting: Navigate to Finance » Membership Plans in the admin dashboard. Click Edit on the target Membership Plan. Search for "Verify Listing" within the plan settings. Enable the option and save the plan. Once enabled, members on that plan will see the verification link and form within their member dashboard. ⚠ NOTE — Setting Is Per Membership Plan: The Verify Listing option must be enabled independently on each Membership Plan where it is required. Enabling it on one plan does not affect any other plans. Part 2 — Member Form Submission After the Verify Listing option is enabled on their plan, the member can access the Listing - Verify Account form from their member dashboard and submit it to request verification. Once submitted, a confirmation message is displayed in the member dashboard. Editing the Form Submission Text Labels The text displayed in the post-submission confirmation message can be edited under Settings » Text Labels . The following three labels control this message: Label Name Description Verification Info Submitted The title or heading displayed after the form is submitted. Verification Paragraph 1 The first paragraph of the post-submission message. Verification Paragraph 2 The second paragraph of the post-submission message. Reference: Settings » Text Labels : Verification Info Submitted : Verification Paragraph 1: Verification Paragraph 2: Viewing Form Submissions Submitted verification requests are stored in the Forms Inbox and can be reviewed by the administrator before a verification decision is made. Reference: Emails » Forms Inbox Customizing the Verification Form Fields The default fields on the Listing - Verify Account form can be edited or extended through the Form Manager. To customize the form: Navigate to Toolbox » Form Manager . Locate the Listing - Verify Account form. Click Actions » Customize . Edit existing fields or add new ones as required. Part 3 — Apply Verified Status to a Member After reviewing a member's form submission, the administrator manually applies the verified status to the member's listing. Navigation Path: Admin Dashboard » My Members » Search Members » Actions » Quick Edit » Listing Settings Tab To verify a member listing: Navigate to My Members » Search Members . Locate the target member in the results table. Click Actions » Quick Edit for that member's record. Navigate to the Listing Settings tab within the Quick Edit module. Locate the Verified Member? setting. Set the value to Verified . Save the change. Post-Verification Message Displayed to the Member Once the administrator has set the member to Verified, a confirmation message is displayed to the member within their dashboard. The text displayed in the post-verification confirmation message can be edited under Settings » Text Labels. The following three labels control this message: Label Name Description Verified Title Label The heading displayed in the verified confirmation message. Verified Paragraph 1 Label The first paragraph of the verified confirmation message. Verified Paragraph 2 Label The second paragraph of the verified confirmation message. Reference : Settings » Text Labels : Verified Title Label : Verified Paragraph 1 Label : Verified Paragraph 2 Label : Part 4 — Send the Verified Confirmation Email Once the member has been set to Verified in the Quick Edit module, the administrator can notify the member by sending the built-in verified confirmation email. The email template to use is: business-listing-verified This template can be customized within the email templates settings before sending. Part 5 — Customization Options Custom Verified Badges The default verified checkmark badge can be replaced with a custom icon to match the visual style of the site. Navigation Path: Admin Dashboard » Settings » General Settings » Brand Images » Verified Member Icon Upload the replacement icon at the path above. Customize the Verify Form URL The URL path where members access the verification form can be changed from its default value. Navigation Path: Admin Dashboard » Settings » Advanced Settings The setting name is Member Verify URL . System variable: default_verify_url The value entered in this field controls the portion of the URL that appears when a member navigates to the verification form from within their dashboard. The default value is promote/verify . Verified Badge Widget — Search Results The verified badge displayed in member search results is controlled by the Bootstrap Theme - Member Verified Badge widget. The badge layout, icon, and text are all editable through this widget and its associated text labels. Reference: How To Customize a Widget Text Labels Controlling the Search Results Badge Two text labels control the content of the verified badge in search results: # Label Name System Variable Controls 1 Search Results Verified Member Icon search_results_verified_member_icon The icon displayed in the badge. 2 Search Results Verified Member search_results_verified_member The text displayed in the badge.

content: Featured Blog Article Slider Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000022422 Overview With the Featured Blog Article Slider add-on it is now possible to hand-select five featured articles to display permanently on a slider on the homepage. title: Understanding SEO Variables
content: Understanding SEO Variables Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000022881 Overview SEO variable names are variables that appear between percent signs ( % ) and are pre-processed before being output to the web page. Several formatting options control how a variable's value is displayed. Percent Sign Formats The examples below use the website_name variable, with a stored value of brilliant directories website (all lowercase). Single Percent Sign Format: %website_name% The variable is output exactly as stored, in lowercase: brilliant directories website . Single Percent Sign + First Capital Letter Format: %Website_name% Capitalizing the first letter of the variable name capitalizes the first letter of each word in the output: Brilliant Directories Website . Double Percent Sign Format: %%website_name%% Wrapping the variable in double percent signs pluralizes the output. Double Percent Sign + First Capital Letter Format: %%Website_name%% Combines both effects — the output is both pluralized and capitalized, following the same capitalization rule described above. Triple Percent Sign Format: %%%website_name%%% The stored value is printed exactly as entered — capital letters remain capital, lowercase letters remain lowercase, with no automatic capitalization or pluralization applied. Postfix Variable Parameters Variable formats can be extended by postfixing them with a method: %variable_name~method% . Regular formatting (single, double, or triple percent signs) still applies when a method is used. Postfix Effect ~ao Pre-processes the variable on the front end only, not for administrators. ~as Adds an apostrophe for possession (e.g., "women" becomes "women's"). ~na Displays the variable name in plain text instead of pre-processing it — %variable_name~na% displays as %variable_name% rather than its value. ~ut Pre-processes the variable and additionally strips special characters (e.g., slashes) to make the output URL-safe. Related Reading The full list of available variables is covered in the " SEO Variables List " article. Special Note Regarding Variable Names SEO variable names should not match an existing database column name, since this creates a naming conflict. The following names should be avoided when naming a custom SEO variable: type , old_filename , new_filename , updated_by , name , icon , keywords , order , group_name , database , first_name , last_name , email , company , phone_number , fax_number , address1 , address2 , zip_code , zip , state_code , country_code , state_ln , country_ln , website , twitter , facebook , linkedin , blog , active , token , position , profession , additional , link , link_order , user_id , comments , data_name , data_type , form , form_name , search_results , h1 , h2 , post_type , widget , widget_name , status , title , section , filename , quote , experience , affiliation , awards , published , education , softwares , fees , about_me , featured , testimonial , preferred , work_experience , rep_matters , speaking_engagements , current_position , additional_fields , lat , lon , post_title , post_caption , post_category , post_image , post_price , post_tags , group_category , property_status , property_type , property_beds , property_baths , property_price

title: Add an Admin Menu Link to a Custom Plugin
content:
Add an Admin Menu Link to a Custom Plugin Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000024699 This article explains how to add a custom plugin to the Plugins menu in the website's Admin area. Plugin menu links are stored in the plugin_records database table. Each record defines a plugin's display name, destination URL, and whether it is active. Database Table Property Value Table Name plugin_records Storage Engine InnoDB Collation utf8_unicode_ci Table Structure The plugin_records table contains the following columns: Column Description plugin_record_id Primary key. active Determines whether the plugin appears in the Admin area ( 1 = Active, 0 = Inactive). variable_name Unique internal identifier for the plugin. nick_name Display name shown in the Plugins menu. link_url URL used to access the plugin. For example: /admin/go.php?widget=XXXXXXXXXXX Creating the plugin_records Table Log in to the website's database. If the plugin_records table does not already exist, run the following SQL statement: Copy CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `plugin_records` (
    `plugin_record_id` bigint( 20 ) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    `active` tinyint( 1 ) NOT NULL ,
    `variable_name` varchar ( 80 ) COLLATE utf8_unicode_ci NOT NULL ,
    `nick_name` varchar ( 80 ) COLLATE utf8_unicode_ci NOT NULL ,
    `link_url` varchar ( 100 ) COLLATE utf8_unicode_ci NOT NULL , PRIMARY KEY (`plugin_record_id`), UNIQUE KEY `variable_name` (`variable_name`)
) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = utf8 COLLATE= utf8_unicode_ci
COMMENT = 'This table stores links to widgets accessed through go.php' AUTO_INCREMENT = 1 ; Adding a Plugin Create a new record in the plugin_records table using the column structure described above. The link_url field accepts a complete URL rather than only a widget name. This allows additional GET parameters to be included when needed. Note: There is currently no Admin interface for managing plugin_records . New records must be added directly to the database. I also made a couple of subtle improvements that align with the style we've been using: Added a proper introduction. Replaced the awkward "Database Structure / Description / Storage Engine / Collation" layout with a clean table. Removed wording like "This table includes..." in favor of direct descriptions. Renamed "How to Create / Add a Plugin..." to the shorter "Adding a Plugin" and "Creating the plugin_records Table." Changed "There is not an UI" to "There is currently no Admin interface..." , which reads much more naturally. Kept all of the technical information intact while making the article easier to scan.

title: How to Change Search Results Sorting Options
content: How to Change Search Results Sorting Options Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000024824 Navigate to MY CONTENT > EDIT POST SETTINGS and click on " Edit " for the post type in which the sorting order will be changed: Move to the Search Results Design tab: Scroll down and expand the Additional Settings and open up the " Order Results By ": Sort Order Options Customizing the sort order for member and post type search results can be found in the Post Settings in the admin dashboard. The available sorting options depend on whether the results are listings/profiles or member-published posts. Member Listings Member Name A-Z Member Name Z-A Member/Post ID (Oldest First) Member/Post ID (Newest First) Sort by Last Name A-Z (If no last name is present, it will use the company name as the last name) Sort by Last Name Z-A (If no last name is present, it will use the company name as the last name) Number of Reviews Random Order * Member Posts Date Posted (Earliest Date Last) Date Posted (Earliest Date First) Start Date (Earliest Date Last) - If Applicable Start Date (Earliest Date First) - If Applicable End Date (Earliest Date Last) - If Applicable End Date (Earliest Date First) - If Applicable Post ID (Smallest to Largest) Post ID (Largest to Smallest) Post Title A - Z Post Title Z - A Advanced - Edit in Search Widget Random Order * Selecting Random Order When the order is set to " Random ", the results will be randomized once and then maintained for all pages of results for that search. Viewing results pages 2, 3, 4, etc of the search will not show newly randomized results - the order will be maintained on all of these pages of results, even when navigating back and forth between them. Once a new search is performed or the user navigates back to the original page of results, the order will be freshly randomized again. The Random option will apply to all types of searches except radius-based location searches, which always order by distance from the searched location. Searching by category, keyword or nothing will have random results. Membership Plan “Search Priority” Additionally, the setting "When Sorting Members - Respect Membership Plan “Search Priority” will respect the "Search Results Priority" logic based on the Membership Plan settings. Location Searches & Sort Order When doing a radius-type location search (cities and zip codes by default) it will return members in order of distance from the searched location. Selecting any of the front-end options will override the distance and results will be returned based on the chosen filter: Search Results Sort Order Options Whenever a search is conducted, the results are automatically filtered and sorted according to the selected option. Additionally, members and visitors can choose their preferred sorting option directly from the front end of the website. There are 6 available filters on the front end: Sort Results Sort by Most Reviews Sort by Name A-Z Sort by Name Z-A Sort By Last Name A-Z Sort By Last Name Z-A Sort Order Text Labels If the admin does not want one of the available sort options to show on the front end, the corresponding Text Label needs to be left blank by deleting the text: These are the text labels that can be edited or deleted: Label Name: Default sort label System Variable: default_sort_label Label Name: Most reviews sort label System Variable: most_reviews_sort_label Label Name: Az sort label System Variable: az_sort_label Label Name: Za sort label System Variable: za_sort_label Please refer to this article to learn more about text labels: Settings » Text Labels In this example, after deleting the text labels for " Sort by Name/Last Name ", these options no longer shows in the front end of the site: Important Note At this time, the ability to compare members in search results on the front end is not available.

title: Toolbox » Widget Manager Overview
content: Toolbox » Widget Manager Overview Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000025507 Widgets are the core components of a Brilliant Directories website. They contain most of the PHP, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that control how the site functions and displays content. Modifying widget code is often required when adjusting layout, functionality, or specific areas of the website. Default Widgets Default Widgets are stored in a central database that all Brilliant Directories websites reference automatically. These widgets remain up-to-date because they are maintained centrally. The internal development team updates Default Widgets to support core functionality, introduce new features, and apply improvements. If no customization is made, the website continues to use the latest version of each Default Widget. Default Widgets can be accessed under Toolbox » Widget Manager in the admin area. Customized Widgets When a Default Widget is customized, or a new widget is created using the New Widget option, it appears in the Customized Widgets section. This section is located at the top of the Toolbox » Widget Manager page, above the Default Widgets list. Edit Widget Tabs Each widget includes three primary code sections: HTML CSS JavaScript Diff Each tab corresponds to its respective language and allows direct editing of the widget code. Diff Tab The Diff tab compares the Default Widget code with the Customized version side by side. The code is separated into collapsible sections: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. This makes it easy to identify exactly what has changed in each area. Each section displays a line count summary (e.g. "10 vs 9 lines (+1)") so it is easy to see how many lines differ. Lines that exist in the customized version but not the default are highlighted, making it simple to pinpoint modifications at a glance. This tab is only available for Customized Widgets. Widget Type The Edit Widget view includes an option to define the widget type. Select "Widget" for standard functionality. Select "Advertisement / Banner" when the widget is intended to display banner content. Note: If "Advertisement / Banner" is selected while the Display Banner Advertisements setting (Design Settings → Banner Ads) is disabled, the widget content will not be displayed. Additional Resources Some useful articles related to widgets can be found below: How To Customize A Widget How To Create A New Widget How To Disable/Enable A Widget How To Delete A Widget Bulk Actions For Widgets How To Call A Widget On A Custom Page Locating The Widgets Via Admin Bar
